simetri.geom.polygons.polygon

Polygon topology and boolean/partition helpers.

Objects here (Node, Edge, Polygon, Partition, …) are not meant to be transformed directly. Each exposes a shape (or group) property that returns a drawable simetri.graphics object.

Examples

import simetri.graphics as sg

    area = sg.polygon_area([(0, 0), (1, 0), (1, 1), (0, 1)])

 137@dataclass
 138class Edge:
 139    """A polygon edge between two ``Node`` endpoints.
 140
 141    Attributes:
 142        nodes: Pair of endpoint nodes.
 143    """
 144
 145    nodes: tuple[Node, Node]
 146    _closed: bool = field(default=False, init=False, repr=False)
 147    _nodes: tuple[Node, Node] = field(init=False, repr=False)
 148
 149    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
 150        self.id: int = get_unique_id(self)
 151
 152    @property
 153    def shape(self) -> Shape:
 154        """Return a two-point ``Shape`` for this edge.
 155
 156        Returns:
 157            Shape: Drawable segment.
 158        """
 159        return _shape([n.pos for n in self.nodes])
 160
 161    @property
 162    def closed(self) -> bool:
 163        """Whether this geometry is closed (always False for an edge).
 164
 165        Returns:
 166            bool: Always False.
 167        """
 168        return self._closed
 169
 170    @property
 171    def nodes(self) -> tuple[Node, Node]:
 172        """Endpoint nodes of the edge.
 173
 174        Returns:
 175            tuple[Node, Node]: Start and end nodes.
 176        """
 177        return self._nodes
 178
 179    @nodes.setter
 180    def nodes(self, value: tuple[Node, Node]) -> None:
 181        """Set endpoint nodes (invalidates cached length).
 182
 183        Args:
 184            value: New ``(start, end)`` node pair.
 185        """
 186        if (
 187            "_nodes" in self.__dict__
 188            and self._nodes != value
 189            and "_length" in self.__dict__
 190        ):
 191            del self._length
 192        self._nodes = value
 193
 194    @property
 195    def length(self) -> float:
 196        """Euclidean length of the edge (cached).
 197
 198        Returns:
 199            float: Edge length.
 200        """
 201        # Used cached value if it exists
 202        if "_length" not in self.__dict__:
 203            a, b = self.nodes
 204            res = distance(a.pos, b.pos)
 205            self._length = res
 206        else:
 207            res = self._length
 208
 209        return res

 257def polygon_area(
 258    polygon: Sequence[PointType], abs_tol: float | None = None
 259) -> float:
 260    """Return the signed area of a polygon.
 261
 262    A counter-clockwise walk is positive. A clockwise walk is negative.
 263    An unclosed ring is closed for the calculation only.
 264
 265    Args:
 266        polygon (Sequence[PointType]): Vertices in walk order.
 267        abs_tol (float | None): Distance used to decide whether the ring
 268            is already closed. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
 269
 270    Returns:
 271        float: Signed area.
 272
 273    Examples:
 274        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 275        >>> sg.polygon_area([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)])
 276        1600.0
 277        >>> sg.polygon_area([(0, 0), (0, 40), (40, 40), (40, 0)])
 278        -1600.0
 279        >>> sg.polygon_area([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40), (0, 0)])
 280        1600.0
 281"""
 282    if abs_tol is None:
 283        abs_tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
 284    abs_tol2 = abs_tol * abs_tol
 285    if not close_points_square(polygon[0], polygon[-1], dist2=abs_tol2):
 286        polygon = list(polygon[:])
 287        polygon.append(polygon[0])
 288    area_ = 0
 289    for i, point in enumerate(polygon[:-1]):
 290        x1, y1 = point[:2]
 291        x2, y2 = polygon[i + 1][:2]
 292        area_ += x1 * y2 - x2 * y1
 293
 294    return area_ / 2
 295

 297def ccw_positive_vertices(
 298    vertices: Sequence[PointType],
 299) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
 300    """Return a counter-clockwise copy of ``vertices``.
 301
 302    A clockwise walk is reversed so the signed area is positive.
 303
 304    Args:
 305        vertices (Sequence[PointType]): Polygon vertices in order.
 306
 307    Returns:
 308        list[tuple[float, float]]: Counter-clockwise vertex copy.
 309
 310    Examples:
 311        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 312        >>> sg.ccw_positive_vertices([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40)])
 313        [(0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0)]
 314        >>> sg.ccw_positive_vertices([(0, 0), (0, 40), (40, 0)])
 315        [(40.0, 0.0), (0.0, 40.0), (0.0, 0.0)]
 316"""
 317    verts = [(float(x), float(y)) for x, y in vertices]
 318    if polygon_area(verts) < 0:
 319        verts = list(reversed(verts))
 320
 321    return verts
 322

 597def _segment_containment_counts(
 598    midpoints: Sequence[PointType],
 599    shape_vertices: Sequence[Sequence[PointType]],
 600) -> NDArray[np.int16]:
 601    """Count how many polygons contain each segment midpoint.
 602
 603    Args:
 604        midpoints (Sequence[PointType]): Points to test.
 605        shape_vertices (Sequence[Sequence[PointType]]): Polygon vertex rings.
 606
 607    Returns:
 608        NDArray[np.int16]: One count per midpoint.
 609
 610    Examples:
 611        >>> from simetri.geom.polygons.polygon import _segment_containment_counts
 612        >>> square = [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
 613        >>> list(_segment_containment_counts([(0.5, 0.5), (80, 80)], [square]))
 614        [1, 0]
 615"""
 616    counts = np.zeros(len(midpoints), dtype=np.int16)
 617    for vertices in shape_vertices:
 618        for index, midpoint_ in enumerate(midpoints):
 619            if in_polygon(midpoint_, vertices):
 620                counts[index] += 1
 621    return counts
 622

 624def point_inside_polygon(
 625    p: PointType, poly: Sequence[PointType], eps: float = 1e-5
 626) -> bool:
 627    """Return True only if ``p`` is strictly inside ``poly``.
 628
 629    Points on the boundary return False.
 630
 631    Args:
 632        p (PointType): Query point ``(x, y)``.
 633        poly (Sequence[PointType]): Ordered polygon vertices.
 634        eps (float): Tolerance for on-segment tests. Defaults to ``1e-5``.
 635
 636    Returns:
 637        bool: True if strictly inside; False on the boundary or outside.
 638
 639    Examples:
 640        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 641        >>> square = [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
 642        >>> sg.point_inside_polygon((0.5, 0.5), square)
 643        True
 644        >>> sg.point_inside_polygon((0.5, 0), square)
 645        False
 646        >>> sg.point_inside_polygon((80, 80), square)
 647        False
 648"""
 649    x, y = p
 650    n = len(poly)
 651
 652    # boundary check
 653    for i in range(n):
 654        a = poly[i]
 655        b = poly[(i + 1) % n]
 656        if on_segment(a, b, p, eps=eps):
 657            return False
 658
 659    inside = False
 660    for i in range(n):
 661        a = poly[i]
 662        b = poly[(i + 1) % n]
 663        ax, ay = a
 664        bx, by = b
 665
 666        # edge straddles horizontal ray?
 667        if (ay > y) != (by > y):
 668            # x intersection
 669            x_int = (bx - ax) * (y - ay) / (by - ay) + ax
 670            if x_int > x + eps:
 671                inside = not inside
 672    return inside
 673

 675def polygons_union(
 676    shapes: Sequence[Shape],
 677    all_segments: Sequence[LineType],
 678    all_midpoints: Sequence[PointType],
 679    min_seg_len: float = 0.001,
 680) -> tuple[Shape, Group]:
 681    """Return the union boundary of polygon shapes from a segment arrangement.
 682
 683    A single shape is returned unchanged, with an empty hole group.
 684    Shared interior edges are dropped. The midpoint of a kept segment
 685    lies in exactly one input polygon.
 686
 687    Args:
 688        shapes (Sequence[Shape]): Input polygon shapes.
 689        all_segments (Sequence[LineType]): Arrangement segments.
 690        all_midpoints (Sequence[PointType]): Midpoints parallel to
 691            ``all_segments``.
 692        min_seg_len (float): Drop segments shorter than this. Defaults
 693            to ``0.001``.
 694
 695    Returns:
 696        tuple[Shape, Group]: Outer union boundary and a group of holes.
 697
 698    Raises:
 699        ValueError: If ``shapes`` is empty.
 700
 701    Examples:
 702        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 703        >>> square = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
 704        >>> outer, holes = sg.polygons_union([square], [], [])
 705        >>> [tuple(round(c, 6) for c in p[:2]) for p in outer.vertices]
 706        [(0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0)]
 707        >>> holes
 708        Group()
 709        >>> sg.polygons_union([], [], [])
 710        Traceback (most recent call last):
 711        ...
 712        ValueError: polygons_union requires at least one polygon
 713"""
 714    if len(shapes) == 0:
 715        raise ValueError("polygons_union requires at least one polygon")
 716    if len(shapes) == 1:
 717        return shapes[0], _group([])
 718
 719    shape_vertices = [shape.vertices for shape in shapes]
 720    counts = _segment_containment_counts(all_midpoints, shape_vertices)
 721
 722    # Keep arrangement segments whose midpoint lies in exactly one input polygon.
 723    # Shared interior edges (count >= 2) and exterior void edges (count == 0)
 724    # are dropped; count == 1 is the union-boundary (XOR) rule.
 725    union_segments = []
 726    for segment, _, count in zip(all_segments, all_midpoints, counts):
 727        if distance(*segment) < min_seg_len:
 728            continue
 729        if count == 1:
 730            union_segments.append(segment)
 731
 732    merged = _group(
 733        [_shape(segment) for segment in union_segments]
 734    ).merge_shapes()
 735    outer = merged[0]
 736    holes = [
 737        part
 738        for part in merged[1:]
 739        if point_inside_polygon(part[-1], outer.vertices)
 740    ]
 741    return outer, _group(holes)
 742
 743
 744def all_close_points(
 745    points: Sequence[Sequence[float]],
 746    abs_tol: float | None = None,
 747    with_dist: bool = False,
 748) -> tuple[
 749    dict[int, Sequence[int]],
 750    Sequence[tuple[int, int] | tuple[int, int, float]],
 751]:
 752    """Return close point ids, and the pairs that produced them.
 753
 754    Each input row is ``[x, y, id]``. Nearby points are linked in both
 755    directions.
 756
 757    Args:
 758        points (Sequence[Sequence[float]]): Rows ``[x, y, id]``.
 759        abs_tol (float | None): Distance tolerance. Defaults to
 760            ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
 761        with_dist (bool): If True, each pair is ``(id1, id2, distance)``.
 762            Defaults to False.
 763
 764    Returns:
 765        tuple: ``({id: [nearby ids], ...}, pairs)``. Ids with no neighbor
 766        are omitted from the dictionary.
 767
 768    Examples:
 769        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 770        >>> rows = [[0, 0, 1], [0.01, 0, 2], [5, 5, 3]]
 771        >>> sg.all_close_points(rows, abs_tol=0.05)
 772        ({1: [2], 2: [1]}, [(1, 2)])
 773        >>> links, pairs = sg.all_close_points(rows, abs_tol=0.05, with_dist=True)
 774        >>> links
 775        {1: [2], 2: [1]}
 776        >>> round(pairs[0][2], 2)
 777        0.01
 778"""
 779    if abs_tol is None:
 780        abs_tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
 781    point_arr = np.array(
 782        points, dtype=np.float32
 783    )  # points array [[x1, y1, id1], ...]]
 784    n_rows = len(points)
 785    point_arr = point_arr[point_arr[:, 0].argsort()]  # sort by x values in the
 786    # first column
 787    xmin = point_arr[:, 0] - abs_tol * 2
 788    xmin = xmin.reshape(n_rows, 1)
 789    xmax = point_arr[:, 0] + abs_tol * 2
 790    xmax = xmax.reshape(n_rows, 1)
 791    point_arr = np.concatenate(
 792        (point_arr, xmin, xmax), 1
 793    )  # [x, y, id, xmin, xmax]
 794
 795    i_id, i_xmin, i_xmax = 2, 3, 4  # column indices
 796    d_connections = {}
 797    for i in range(n_rows):
 798        d_connections[int(point_arr[i, 2])] = []
 799    pairs = []
 800    abs_tol2 = abs_tol * abs_tol
 801    for i in range(n_rows):
 802        x, y, id1, sl_xmin, sl_xmax = point_arr[i, :]
 803        id1 = int(id1)
 804        point = (x, y)
 805        start = i + 1
 806        candidates = point_arr[start:, :][
 807            (
 808                (point_arr[start:, i_xmax] >= sl_xmin)
 809                & (point_arr[start:, i_xmin] <= sl_xmax)
 810            )
 811        ]
 812        for cand in candidates:
 813            id2 = int(cand[i_id])
 814            point2 = cand[:2]
 815            if close_points_square(point, point2, dist2=abs_tol2):
 816                d_connections[id1].append(id2)
 817                d_connections[id2].append(id1)
 818                if with_dist:
 819                    pairs.append((id1, id2, distance(point, point2)))
 820                else:
 821                    pairs.append((id1, id2))
 822    res = {node_id: connections for node_id, connections in d_connections.items() if connections}
 823    return res, pairs
 824
 825
 826def node_dictionaries(
 827    coords: Sequence[PointType],
 828    abs_tol: float,
 829    debug: bool = False,
 830) -> tuple[
 831    dict[int, tuple[float, ...]],
 832    dict[tuple[float, ...], int],
 833    dict[tuple[float, ...], PointType],
 834]:
 835    """Return node maps for coordinates that fall within ``abs_tol``.
 836
 837    Nearby coordinates share one node id. The third map keeps the original
 838    coordinate for each rounded key.
 839
 840    Args:
 841        coords (Sequence[PointType]): Vertices to index.
 842        abs_tol (float): Distance used to merge nearby coordinates.
 843        debug (bool): If True, print the closest unmerged pair.
 844            Defaults to False.
 845
 846    Returns:
 847        tuple: ``(node_to_coord, coord_to_node, rounded_to_original)``.
 848
 849    Examples:
 850        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 851        >>> nodes, coord_node, rounded = sg.node_dictionaries(
 852        ... [(0, 0), (0.01, 0), (20, 20)], 0.05
 853        ... )
 854        >>> nodes
 855        {0: (0, 0), 1: (20, 20)}
 856        >>> coord_node[(0, 0)] == coord_node[(0.01, 0)]
 857        True
 858        >>> rounded[(20, 20)]
 859        (20, 20)
 860"""
 861    n_round = max(0, ceil(log10(sqrt(2) / abs_tol)))
 862    d_rounded_coord = {}
 863    rounded = []
 864    for coord in coords:
 865        val = tuple(round_point(coord, n_round))
 866        rounded.append(val)
 867        d_rounded_coord[val] = coord
 868
 869    rounded_coords = list(set(rounded))
 870    rounded_coords.sort()
 871    rounded_coords.sort(key=lambda point: point[1])
 872
 873    indexed_coordinates = [
 874        (*coordinate[:2], index)
 875        for index, coordinate in enumerate(rounded_coords)
 876    ]
 877    _, close_pairs = all_close_points(indexed_coordinates, abs_tol=abs_tol)
 878    parent = list(range(len(rounded_coords)))
 879    for first_index, second_index in close_pairs:
 880        first_root = first_index
 881        while parent[first_root] != first_root:
 882            first_root = parent[first_root]
 883        second_root = second_index
 884        while parent[second_root] != second_root:
 885            second_root = parent[second_root]
 886        if first_root != second_root:
 887            parent[second_root] = first_root
 888
 889    d_node_coord = {}
 890    d_coord_node = {}
 891
 892    root_node = {}
 893    for coordinate_index, coordinate in enumerate(rounded_coords):
 894        root = coordinate_index
 895        while parent[root] != root:
 896            root = parent[root]
 897        if root not in root_node:
 898            node = len(root_node)
 899            root_node[root] = node
 900            d_node_coord[node] = rounded_coords[root]
 901        d_coord_node[coordinate] = root_node[root]
 902
 903    if debug:
 904        closest_distance = None
 905        closest_points = None
 906        for first_point, second_point in combinations(coords, 2):
 907            first_coordinate = tuple(round_point(first_point, n_round))
 908            second_coordinate = tuple(round_point(second_point, n_round))
 909            if (
 910                d_coord_node[first_coordinate]
 911                == d_coord_node[second_coordinate]
 912            ):
 913                continue
 914            point_distance = distance(first_point, second_point)
 915            if closest_distance is None or point_distance < closest_distance:
 916                closest_distance = point_distance
 917                closest_points = (first_point[:2], second_point[:2])
 918        print(
 919            "Node diagnostics: "
 920            f"abs_tol={abs_tol}; automatic n_round={n_round}; "
 921            f"nodes={len(d_node_coord)}"
 922        )
 923        print(
 924            "  Closest unmerged point distance: "
 925            f"{closest_distance}; points={closest_points}"
 926        )
 927
 928    return (d_node_coord, d_coord_node, d_rounded_coord)
 929
 930
 931def segment_cycles(
 932    segments: Sequence[LineType],
 933    length_bound: int = 10,
 934    cycle_basis: bool = False,
 935    abs_tol: float | None = None,
 936) -> tuple[list, list]:
 937    """Return closed walks formed by line segments.
 938
 939    Args:
 940        segments (Sequence[LineType]): Segments ``[(p1, p2), ...]``.
 941        length_bound (int): Maximum cycle length. Defaults to 10.
 942        cycle_basis (bool): If True, use a cycle basis. Defaults to False.
 943        abs_tol (float | None): Distance for merging nearby endpoints.
 944            Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
 945
 946    Returns:
 947        tuple: ``(coordinate_cycles, node_id_cycles)``.
 948
 949    Examples:
 950        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 951        >>> square = [
 952        ... ((0, 0), (40, 0)),
 953        ... ((40, 0), (40, 40)),
 954        ... ((40, 40), (0, 40)),
 955        ... ((0, 40), (0, 0)),
 956        ... ]
 957        >>> coords, nodes = sg.segment_cycles(square)
 958        >>> coords
 959        [[(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]]
 960        >>> len(nodes[0])
 961        4
 962"""
 963    if abs_tol is None:
 964        abs_tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
 965    coordinates = []
 966    for seg in segments:
 967        coordinates.extend(seg)
 968
 969    d_node_coord, d_coord_node, _ = node_dictionaries(coordinates, abs_tol)
 970    n_round = max(0, ceil(log10(sqrt(2) / abs_tol)))
 971    g_segments = [
 972        [d_coord_node[tuple(round_point(coord, n_round))] for coord in seg]
 973        for seg in segments
 974    ]
 975
 976    nx_graph = nx.Graph()
 977    nx_graph.update(g_segments)
 978    if cycle_basis:
 979        cycles = [
 980            cycle
 981            for cycle in nx.cycle_basis(nx_graph)
 982            if len(cycle) <= length_bound
 983        ]
 984    else:
 985        cycles = list(nx.simple_cycles(nx_graph, length_bound=length_bound))
 986    res = [[d_node_coord[node] for node in cycle] for cycle in cycles]
 987
 988    return res, cycles
 989
 990
 991def segments_from_points(
 992    points: Sequence[PointType],
 993) -> tuple[PointType, PointType] | None:
 994    """Return consecutive segments after sorting collinear points.
 995
 996    Args:
 997        points (Sequence[PointType]): Collinear points in any order.
 998
 999    Returns:
1000        list[tuple[PointType, PointType]] | None: Sorted segments, or
1001        ``None`` if fewer than two points are given.
1002
1003    Examples:
1004        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1005        >>> sg.segments_from_points([(80, 0), (0, 0), (40, 0)])
1006        [((0, 0), (40, 0)), ((40, 0), (80, 0))]
1007        >>> sg.segments_from_points([(0, 0), (40, 0)])
1008        [((0, 0), (40, 0))]
1009        >>> sg.segments_from_points([(0, 0)]) is None
1010        True
1011"""
1012    n = len(points)
1013    if n < 2:
1014        res = None
1015    elif n == 2:
1016        res = [tuple(points)]
1017    else:
1018        sorted_points = sorted(points, key=lambda p: (p[0], p[1]))
1019        segments = list(pairwise(sorted_points))
1020        res = segments
1021
1022    return res
1023
1024
1025def set_fills(
1026    partitions: Sequence[Shape], d_edge_part: dict[frozenset, set[int]]
1027) -> None:
1028    """Set each partition's fill from the symmetric-difference rule.
1029
1030    An outer partition, one that owns an edge alone, is filled. Across a
1031    shared edge the neighboring fill is the opposite value.
1032
1033    Args:
1034        partitions (Sequence[Shape]): Closed partition shapes (mutated).
1035        d_edge_part (dict[frozenset, set[int]]): Edge to partition-id map.
1036
1037    Returns:
1038        None: Fills are written onto the partition objects.
1039
1040    Examples:
1041        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1042        >>> outer = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (80, 0), (80, 80), (0, 80)], closed=True)
1043        >>> edges = {frozenset(edge): {outer.id} for edge in outer.edges}
1044        >>> sg.set_fills([outer], edges)
1045        >>> outer.fill
1046        True
1047"""
1048
1049    # To start, find an edge with a single partition.
1050    # and the partition to the queue.
1051    # This is one of the outermost partitions.
1052    # Since outer partitions are always filled,
1053    # set this partition's fill property True.
1054    for edge, part in d_edge_part.items():
1055        if len(part) == 1:
1056            cur_part = d_id_obj[next(iter(part))]
1057            queue = {cur_part.id}
1058            cur_part.fill = True
1059            break
1060    # If an edge is between two partitions,
1061    # only one partition can be filled.
1062    # Alternate through all partitions.
1063    processed = set()
1064    count = 0
1065    qcount = 0
1066    while queue:
1067        count += 1
1068        cur_part = d_id_obj[queue.pop()]
1069        count += 1
1070        if cur_part.id not in processed:
1071            qcount += 1
1072            edges = [frozenset(e) for e in cur_part.edges]
1073            for edge in edges:
1074                partitions = d_edge_part[edge]
1075                if len(partitions) == 2:
1076                    part1, part2 = [d_id_obj[p] for p in partitions]
1077                    fill = not cur_part.fill
1078                    if part1 == cur_part:
1079                        part2.fill = fill
1080                    else:
1081                        part1.fill = fill
1082
1083                queue.update(set(partitions))
1084            processed.add(cur_part.id)
1085            queue.difference_update(processed)
1086
1087
1088def any_point_inside_polygon(
1089    points: Sequence[PointType],
1090    polygon: Shape | NDArray,
1091    eps: float = 1e-12,
1092) -> bool:
1093    """Return True if any point is strictly inside the polygon.
1094
1095    Boundary points are treated as outside.
1096
1097    Args:
1098        points (Sequence[PointType]): Query points ``(x, y)``.
1099        polygon (Shape | NDArray): Closed vertex ring, or a closed ``Shape``.
1100        eps (float): Tolerance for on-edge tests. Defaults to ``1e-12``.
1101
1102    Returns:
1103        bool: True if at least one point is inside and not on the boundary.
1104
1105    Examples:
1106        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1107        >>> square = [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
1108        >>> sg.any_point_inside_polygon([(80, 80), (0.2, 0.2)], square)
1109        True
1110        >>> sg.any_point_inside_polygon([(80, 80), (60, 60)], square)
1111        False
1112        >>> sg.any_point_inside_polygon([(0.5, 0)], square)
1113        False
1114"""
1115
1116    pts = np.asarray(points, dtype=float)
1117    poly = np.asarray(polygon, dtype=float)
1118
1119    px = pts[:, 0][:, None]  # (M,1)
1120    py = pts[:, 1][:, None]
1121
1122    x1 = poly[:, 0]
1123    y1 = poly[:, 1]
1124    x2 = np.roll(x1, -1)
1125    y2 = np.roll(y1, -1)
1126
1127    # -----------------------------
1128    # Boundary detection (on edge)
1129    # -----------------------------
1130    cross = (py - y1) * (x2 - x1) - (px - x1) * (y2 - y1)
1131
1132    on_seg = (
1133        (np.abs(cross) < eps)
1134        & (np.minimum(x1, x2) <= px)
1135        & (px <= np.maximum(x1, x2))
1136        & (np.minimum(y1, y2) <= py)
1137        & (py <= np.maximum(y1, y2))
1138    )
1139
1140    # Any point on boundary is NOT considered inside
1141    on_boundary = np.any(on_seg, axis=1)
1142
1143    # -----------------------------
1144    # Ray casting (interior test)
1145    # -----------------------------
1146    cond = (y1 > py) != (y2 > py)
1147    x_intersect = (x2 - x1) * (py - y1) / (y2 - y1 + 1e-15) + x1
1148
1149    inside = np.sum(cond & (px < x_intersect), axis=1) % 2 == 1
1150
1151    # Exclude boundary points from interior
1152    inside_strict = inside & (~on_boundary)
1153
1154    return np.any(inside_strict)
1155
1156
1157def get_partitions(
1158    shapes: Group, length_bound: int = 10
1159) -> tuple[Sequence[Shape], defaultdict[frozenset, set[int]], Shape]:
1160    """Partition overlapping shapes into face regions from their arrangement.
1161
1162    Prints cycle and hole counts while it runs.
1163
1164    Args:
1165        shapes (Group): Group whose segments define the arrangement.
1166        length_bound (int): Maximum cycle length when enumerating faces.
1167            Defaults to 10.
1168
1169    Returns:
1170        tuple: ``(partition_shapes, membership_map, merged_outline)``.
1171
1172    Examples:
1173        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1174        >>> square = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1175        >>> parts, _, outline = sg.get_partitions(sg.Group([square]))
1176        Number of total cycles with less than 10 nodes: 5
1177        Number of holes: 0
1178        Total partition-area: 1600.00, Union-area: 1600.00
1179        5 partitions.
1180        Largest* partition has 4 edges.
1181        Used 5 cycles.
1182        >>> [tuple(round(c, 6) for c in p[:2]) for p in outline.vertices]
1183        [(0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0)]
1184"""
1185    n_edges = len(shapes.all_segments)
1186    intersections = all_intersections(
1187        shapes.all_segments, return_points_list=True
1188    )
1189    points_by_edge = defaultdict(list)
1190    for edge_id, edge in enumerate(shapes.all_segments):
1191        start_point, end_point = edge
1192        points_by_edge[edge_id].extend(
1193            (round_point(start_point), round_point(end_point))
1194        )
1195    for point, (first_edge_id, second_edge_id) in intersections:
1196        rounded_point = round_point(point)
1197        points_by_edge[first_edge_id].append(rounded_point)
1198        points_by_edge[second_edge_id].append(rounded_point)
1199
1200    all_segments = []
1201    all_midpoints = []
1202    for i in range(n_edges):
1203        points = points_by_edge[i]
1204        if len(points) >= 2:
1205            segments = segments_from_points(points)
1206            rounded_segments = [round_segment(seg, 2) for seg in segments]
1207            all_segments.extend(rounded_segments)
1208            all_midpoints.extend(
1209                midpoint(*segment) for segment in rounded_segments
1210            )
1211
1212    midpoint_array = np.unique(np.asarray(all_midpoints, dtype=float), axis=0)
1213    midpoint_order = midpoint_array[:, 0].argsort()
1214    midpoint_array = midpoint_array[midpoint_order]
1215
1216    cycles, cycles_nodes = segment_cycles(
1217        all_segments, length_bound=length_bound
1218    )
1219
1220    print(
1221        f"Number of total cycles with less than {length_bound} nodes: {len(cycles)}"
1222    )
1223    sorted_cycles = sorted(
1224        zip(cycles, cycles_nodes), key=lambda cycle_pair: len(cycle_pair[0])
1225    )
1226    cycles = [cycle_pair[0] for cycle_pair in sorted_cycles]
1227    cycles_nodes = [cycle_pair[1] for cycle_pair in sorted_cycles]
1228    union, holes = polygons_union(shapes, all_segments, all_midpoints)
1229    print(f"Number of holes: {len(holes)}")
1230    holes_area = sum([polygon_area(hole.vertices) for hole in holes])
1231    union_area = polygon_area(union.vertices) - holes_area
1232    hole_index, sorted_hole_arrays, hole_processed = _build_hole_index(holes)
1233    abs_tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
1234
1235    count = 0
1236    area = 0
1237    partitions = []
1238    d_edge_partition = defaultdict(set)
1239    done = False
1240    for poly in cycles:
1241        if done:
1242            break
1243        polygon_array = np.asarray(poly, dtype=float)
1244        polygon_min_x = polygon_array[:, 0].min()
1245        polygon_max_x = polygon_array[:, 0].max()
1246        polygon_min_y = polygon_array[:, 1].min()
1247        polygon_max_y = polygon_array[:, 1].max()
1248        midpoint_start = np.searchsorted(
1249            midpoint_array[:, 0], polygon_min_x, side="left"
1250        )
1251        midpoint_end = np.searchsorted(
1252            midpoint_array[:, 0], polygon_max_x, side="right"
1253        )
1254        candidate_midpoints = midpoint_array[midpoint_start:midpoint_end]
1255        candidate_midpoints = candidate_midpoints[
1256            (candidate_midpoints[:, 1] >= polygon_min_y)
1257            & (candidate_midpoints[:, 1] <= polygon_max_y)
1258        ]
1259        if not any_point_inside_polygon(candidate_midpoints, polygon_array):
1260            count += 1
1261            sorted_partition = sorted_polygon_xy_array(poly)
1262            candidate_hole_ids = _candidate_hole_ids(
1263                hole_index,
1264                hole_processed,
1265                polygon_min_x,
1266                polygon_min_y,
1267                polygon_max_x,
1268                polygon_max_y,
1269                abs_tol,
1270            )
1271            is_hole = False
1272            for hole_id in candidate_hole_ids:
1273                if equal_sorted_arrays(
1274                    sorted_partition,
1275                    sorted_hole_arrays[hole_id],
1276                    abs_tol,
1277                ):
1278                    is_hole = True
1279                    hole_processed[hole_id] = True
1280                    break
1281            if is_hole:
1282                continue
1283            partition = _shape(poly, closed=True)
1284            partitions.append(partition)
1285            for edge in partition.edges:
1286                d_edge_partition[frozenset(edge)].add(partition.id)
1287            poly_area = abs(
1288                polygon_area(poly)
1289            )  # Here, we are not strict about polygons' orientation
1290            area += poly_area
1291
1292            if isclose(area, union_area, rel_tol=0.001):
1293                print(
1294                    f"Total partition-area: {area:.2f}, Union-area: {union_area:.2f}"
1295                )
1296                done = True
1297
1298    print(f"{len(partitions)} partitions.")
1299    n = max((len(p) for p in partitions), default=0)
1300    print(f"Largest* partition has {n} edges.")
1301    print(f"Used {count} cycles.")
1302
1303    return partitions, d_edge_partition, union
1304
1305
1306def equal_sorted_arrays(
1307    array1: NDArray[np.float64],
1308    array2: NDArray[np.float64],
1309    abs_tol: float,
1310) -> bool:
1311    """Return True if two same-shaped point arrays match within ``abs_tol``.
1312
1313    Args:
1314        array1 (NDArray[np.float64]): First ``(n, 2)`` point array.
1315        array2 (NDArray[np.float64]): Second ``(n, 2)`` point array.
1316        abs_tol (float): Maximum allowed per-point distance.
1317
1318    Returns:
1319        bool: True if every corresponding pair is within tolerance.
1320
1321    Examples:
1322        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1323        >>> square = [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
1324        >>> same = [(40, 40), (0, 40), (0, 0), (40, 0)]
1325        >>> sg.equal_sorted_arrays(
1326        ... sg.sorted_polygon_xy_array(square),
1327        ... sg.sorted_polygon_xy_array(same),
1328        ... 0.05,
1329        ... )
1330        True
1331        >>> sg.equal_sorted_arrays(
1332        ... sg.sorted_polygon_xy_array(square),
1333        ... sg.sorted_polygon_xy_array([(0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 80)]),
1334        ... 0.05,
1335        ... )
1336        False
1337"""
1338    if array1.shape != array2.shape:
1339        return False
1340    n_vertices = array1.shape[0]
1341    if n_vertices == 0:
1342        return True
1343    abs_tol2 = abs_tol * abs_tol
1344    if n_vertices <= 12:
1345        for index in range(n_vertices):
1346            dx = array1[index, 0] - array2[index, 0]
1347            dy = array1[index, 1] - array2[index, 1]
1348            if dx * dx + dy * dy > abs_tol2:
1349                return False
1350        return True
1351    delta = array1 - array2
1352
1353    return bool(np.all((delta * delta).sum(axis=1) <= abs_tol2))
1354
1355
1356_HOLE_DTYPE = np.dtype(
1357    [
1358        ("xmin", np.float64),
1359        ("ymin", np.float64),
1360        ("xmax", np.float64),
1361        ("ymax", np.float64),
1362        ("x", object),
1363        ("y", object),
1364        ("hole_id", np.int64),
1365    ]
1366)
1367
1368
1369def _build_hole_index(
1370    holes: Sequence[Shape],
1371) -> tuple[NDArray[Any], Sequence[NDArray[np.float64]], NDArray[np.bool_]]:
1372    """Build a bbox and sorted-vertex index for hole lookup.
1373
1374    Args:
1375        holes (Sequence[Shape]): Hole shapes to index.
1376
1377    Returns:
1378        tuple: ``(hole_index, sorted_hole_arrays, unused_mask)``.
1379
1380    Examples:
1381        >>> from simetri.geom.polygons.polygon import _build_hole_index
1382        >>> index, arrays, unused = _build_hole_index([])
1383        >>> len(index), arrays, list(unused)
1384        (0, [], [])
1385"""
1386    n_holes = len(holes)
1387    hole_dtype = _HOLE_DTYPE
1388    if n_holes == 0:
1389        return np.empty(0, dtype=hole_dtype), [], np.zeros(0, dtype=bool)
1390
1391    sorted_hole_arrays = [sorted_polygon_xy_array(hole) for hole in holes]
1392    hole_index = np.empty(n_holes, dtype=hole_dtype)
1393    for hole_id, sorted_xy in enumerate(sorted_hole_arrays):
1394        hole_index[hole_id] = (
1395            sorted_xy[:, 0].min(),
1396            sorted_xy[:, 1].min(),
1397            sorted_xy[:, 0].max(),
1398            sorted_xy[:, 1].max(),
1399            sorted_xy[:, 0].copy(),
1400            sorted_xy[:, 1].copy(),
1401            hole_id,
1402        )
1403
1404    return hole_index, sorted_hole_arrays, np.zeros(n_holes, dtype=bool)
1405
1406
1407def _candidate_hole_ids(
1408    hole_index: NDArray[Any],
1409    hole_processed: NDArray[np.bool_],
1410    xmin: float,
1411    ymin: float,
1412    xmax: float,
1413    ymax: float,
1414    abs_tol: float,
1415) -> NDArray[np.int_]:
1416    """Return hole ids whose bbox matches the given bounds within abs_tol.
1417
1418    Args:
1419        hole_index (NDArray[Any]): Index from :func:`_build_hole_index`.
1420        hole_processed (NDArray[np.bool_]): Holes already claimed.
1421        xmin (float): Candidate minimum x.
1422        ymin (float): Candidate minimum y.
1423        xmax (float): Candidate maximum x.
1424        ymax (float): Candidate maximum y.
1425        abs_tol (float): Absolute tolerance for bbox matching.
1426
1427    Returns:
1428        NDArray[np.int_]: Matching hole ids.
1429
1430    Examples:
1431        >>> from simetri.geom.polygons.polygon import (
1432        ... _build_hole_index,
1433        ... _candidate_hole_ids,
1434        ... )
1435        >>> index, _, unused = _build_hole_index([])
1436        >>> list(_candidate_hole_ids(index, unused, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0.05))
1437        []
1438"""
1439    if len(hole_index) == 0:
1440        return np.array([], dtype=int)
1441    mask = (
1442        ~hole_processed
1443        & np.isclose(hole_index["xmin"], xmin, atol=abs_tol)
1444        & np.isclose(hole_index["ymin"], ymin, atol=abs_tol)
1445        & np.isclose(hole_index["xmax"], xmax, atol=abs_tol)
1446        & np.isclose(hole_index["ymax"], ymax, atol=abs_tol)
1447    )
1448
1449    return hole_index["hole_id"][mask].astype(int)
1450
1451
1452def polygon_xy_array(
1453    polygon: Shape | Sequence[PointType] | NDArray[Any],
1454) -> NDArray[np.float64]:
1455    """Return an ``(n, 2)`` float array of polygon xy coordinates.
1456
1457    Args:
1458        polygon (Shape | Sequence[PointType] | NDArray[Any]): A ``Shape``,
1459            point sequence, or array-like.
1460
1461    Returns:
1462        NDArray[np.float64]: XY coordinates. A ``Shape`` uses
1463        ``final_coords``.
1464
1465    Examples:
1466        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1467        >>> [tuple(row) for row in sg.polygon_xy_array([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40)])]
1468        [(0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0)]
1469        >>> sg.polygon_xy_array([(60, 80)]).shape
1470        (1, 2)
1471"""
1472    from simetri.shapes.shape import Shape
1473
1474    if isinstance(polygon, Shape):
1475        # final_coords is the cached primary_points @ xform_matrix result
1476        return polygon.final_coords[:, :2]
1477    array = np.asarray(polygon, dtype=float)
1478    if array.ndim == 1:
1479        array = array.reshape(1, -1)
1480
1481    return array[:, :2]
1482
1483
1484def sorted_polygon_xy_array(
1485    polygon: Shape | Sequence[PointType] | NDArray[Any],
1486) -> NDArray[np.float64]:
1487    """Return polygon xy coordinates sorted by ``x`` then ``y``.
1488
1489    Args:
1490        polygon (Shape | Sequence[PointType] | NDArray[Any]): A ``Shape``,
1491            point sequence, or array-like.
1492
1493    Returns:
1494        NDArray[np.float64]: Lexicographically sorted XY coordinates.
1495
1496    Examples:
1497        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1498        >>> [tuple(row) for row in sg.sorted_polygon_xy_array([(40, 40), (0, 0), (0, 40)])]
1499        [(0.0, 0.0), (0.0, 40.0), (40.0, 40.0)]
1500"""
1501    array = polygon_xy_array(polygon)
1502    order = np.lexsort((array[:, 1], array[:, 0]))
1503
1504    return array[order]
1505
1506
1507def polygon_vertices(polygon: PolygonLike) -> Sequence[PointType]:
1508    """Return vertices from a ``Shape``, or the point sequence itself.
1509
1510    Args:
1511        polygon (PolygonLike): A ``Shape`` or a sequence of points. Groups
1512            are not accepted.
1513
1514    Returns:
1515        Sequence[PointType]: Vertex coordinates.
1516
1517    Examples:
1518        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1519        >>> sg.polygon_vertices([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)])
1520        [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
1521        >>> shape = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 80)], closed=True)
1522        >>> sg.polygon_vertices(shape)
1523        ((0.0, 0.0), (80.0, 0.0), (0.0, 80.0))
1524"""
1525    from ...shapes.shape import Shape
1526
1527    if isinstance(polygon, Shape):
1528        res = polygon.vertices
1529    else:
1530        res = polygon
1531
1532    return res
1533
1534
1535def polygon_turns(vertices: Sequence[PointType]) -> list[float]:
1536    """Return the signed turn sequence of a polygon.
1537
1538    For each vertex, records the outgoing edge length and the signed turn
1539    angle at the next vertex. Angles are rounded to
1540    ``runtime_defaults["turn_angle_digits"]``.
1541
1542    Args:
1543        vertices (Sequence[PointType]): Polygon vertices in walk order.
1544            The first vertex is not repeated.
1545
1546    Returns:
1547        list[float]: Alternating side lengths and turn angles.
1548
1549    Examples:
1550        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1551        >>> sg.polygon_turns([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)])
1552        [40.0, -1.57, 40.0, -1.57, 40.0, -1.57, 40.0, -1.57]
1553        >>> sg.polygon_turns([(0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 40)])
1554        [80.0, -0.46, 89.44271909999159, -1.11, 40.0, -1.57]
1555"""
1556    n = len(vertices)
1557    res = []
1558    TURN_ANGLE_DIGITS = runtime_defaults["turn_angle_digits"]
1559    for i in range(n):
1560        vert = vertices[i]
1561        next_vert = vertices[(i + 1) % n]
1562        next_seg = (next_vert, vertices[(i + 2) % n])
1563        seg = (vert, next_vert)
1564        angle = angle_between_lines3(vert, *next_seg)
1565        res.append(distance(*seg))
1566        res.append(round(angle, TURN_ANGLE_DIGITS))
1567
1568    return res
1569
1570
1571def rotate_turns_to_min_edge(turns: Sequence[float]) -> list[float]:
1572    """Rotate a flat ``[length, angle, ...]`` cycle to start at a shortest edge.
1573
1574    Args:
1575        turns (Sequence[float]): Alternating edge lengths and turn angles.
1576
1577    Returns:
1578        list[float]: Cycle starting at the shortest edge.
1579
1580    Examples:
1581        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1582        >>> sg.rotate_turns_to_min_edge([3.0, 1.57, 1.0, 1.57, 2.0, 1.57])
1583        [1.0, 1.57, 2.0, 1.57, 3.0, 1.57]
1584        >>> sg.rotate_turns_to_min_edge([1.0])
1585        [1.0]
1586"""
1587    if len(turns) < 2:
1588        return list(turns)
1589    n_edges = len(turns) // 2
1590    min_i = min(range(n_edges), key=lambda i: turns[2 * i])
1591    start = 2 * min_i
1592    return list(turns[start:]) + list(turns[:start])
1593
1594
1595def congruent_polygons(
1596    polygon1: PolygonLike,
1597    polygon2: PolygonLike,
1598    mirror: bool = False,
1599    rel_tol: float | None = None,
1600    abs_tol: float | None = None,
1601) -> bool:
1602    """Return True if ``polygon1`` and ``polygon2`` are congruent.
1603
1604    Congruence ignores translation and rotation. Signed turn sequences are
1605    compared cyclically so convex and reflex corners stay distinct.
1606
1607    Args:
1608        polygon1 (PolygonLike): First polygon as a ``Shape`` or points.
1609        polygon2 (PolygonLike): Second polygon as a ``Shape`` or points.
1610        mirror (bool): If True, a reflection also counts as congruent.
1611        rel_tol (float | None): Relative tolerance for turn comparison.
1612            Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["rel_tol"]``.
1613        abs_tol (float | None): Absolute tolerance for turn comparison.
1614            Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
1615
1616    Returns:
1617        bool: True if the polygons are congruent.
1618
1619    Examples:
1620        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1621        >>> square = [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
1622        >>> sg.congruent_polygons(square, [(40, 40), (80, 40), (80, 80), (40, 80)])
1623        True
1624        >>> sg.congruent_polygons(square, [(0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 80)])
1625        False
1626"""
1627    from ...helpers.utilities import equal_cycles
1628
1629    rel_tol, abs_tol = get_defaults(["rel_tol", "abs_tol"], [rel_tol, abs_tol])
1630    verts1 = polygon_vertices(polygon1)
1631    verts2 = polygon_vertices(polygon2)
1632    if len(verts1) != len(verts2):
1633        res = False
1634    else:
1635        poly1_turns = polygon_turns(verts1)
1636        poly2_turns = polygon_turns(verts2)
1637
1638        if mirror:
1639            if equal_cycles(poly1_turns, poly2_turns, rel_tol, abs_tol):
1640                res = True
1641            else:
1642                poly2_turns.reverse()
1643                res = equal_cycles(poly1_turns, poly2_turns, rel_tol, abs_tol)
1644        else:
1645            res = equal_cycles(poly1_turns, poly2_turns, rel_tol, abs_tol)
1646
1647    return res
1648
1649
1650def equal_polygons(
1651    polygon1: PolygonLike,
1652    polygon2: PolygonLike,
1653    mirror: bool = False,
1654    rel_tol: float | None = None,
1655    abs_tol: float | None = None,
1656) -> bool:
1657    """Return True if two polygons are congruent.
1658
1659    This is an alias of :func:`congruent_polygons`.
1660
1661    Args:
1662        polygon1 (PolygonLike): First polygon.
1663        polygon2 (PolygonLike): Second polygon.
1664        mirror (bool): If True, a reflection also counts. Defaults to False.
1665        rel_tol (float | None): Relative tolerance for turn comparison.
1666            Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["rel_tol"]``.
1667        abs_tol (float | None): Absolute tolerance for turn comparison.
1668            Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
1669
1670    Returns:
1671        bool: True when the polygons match under congruence.
1672
1673    Examples:
1674        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1675        >>> square = [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
1676        >>> sg.equal_polygons(square, [(40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40), (0, 0)])
1677        True
1678        >>> sg.equal_polygons(square, [(0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 80)])
1679        False
1680"""
1681    return congruent_polygons(polygon1, polygon2, mirror, rel_tol, abs_tol)
1682
1683
1684def congruent_shapes(
1685    shape1: Shape,
1686    shape2: Shape,
1687    mirror: bool = False,
1688) -> bool:
1689    """Return True if ``shape1`` and ``shape2`` are congruent.
1690
1691    Args:
1692        shape1 (Shape): First shape.
1693        shape2 (Shape): Second shape.
1694        mirror (bool): If True, a reflection also counts as congruent.
1695
1696    Returns:
1697        bool: True if the shapes are congruent.
1698
1699    Examples:
1700        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1701        >>> left = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1702        >>> right = sg.Shape([(40, 0), (80, 0), (80, 40), (40, 40)], closed=True)
1703        >>> sg.congruent_shapes(left, right)
1704        True
1705        >>> other = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 80)], closed=True)
1706        >>> sg.congruent_shapes(left, other)
1707        False
1708"""
1709    return congruent_polygons(shape1, shape2, mirror=mirror)
1710
1711
1712def remove_duplicate_edges(
1713    edges: Sequence[LineType],
1714    keep_one: bool = False,
1715) -> list[LineType]:
1716    """Return edges with congruent duplicates handled.
1717
1718    Candidates are filtered by axis-aligned bounding-box overlap before
1719    ``equal_edges``.
1720
1721    Args:
1722        edges (Sequence[LineType]): Segments ``(point1, point2)``.
1723        keep_one (bool): If True, keep the first copy of each congruent
1724            edge. If False, drop every edge that has a congruent duplicate.
1725
1726    Returns:
1727        list[LineType]: Selected edges.
1728
1729    Examples:
1730        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1731        >>> edges = [((0, 0), (40, 0)), ((40, 0), (0, 0)), ((0, 40), (40, 40))]
1732        >>> sg.remove_duplicate_edges(edges)
1733        [((0, 40), (40, 40))]
1734        >>> sg.remove_duplicate_edges(edges, keep_one=True)
1735        [((0, 0), (40, 0)), ((0, 40), (40, 40))]
1736"""
1737    abs_tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
1738
1739    if not keep_one:
1740        n = len(edges)
1741        if n == 0:
1742            res = []
1743        else:
1744            bboxes = np.empty((n, 4), dtype=float)
1745            for i, edge in enumerate(edges):
1746                x1, y1 = edge[0][:2]
1747                x2, y2 = edge[1][:2]
1748                bboxes[i] = [
1749                    min(x1, x2),
1750                    min(y1, y2),
1751                    max(x1, x2),
1752                    max(y1, y2),
1753                ]
1754
1755            duplicate_mask = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)
1756            for i in range(n):
1757                min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y = bboxes[i]
1758                overlap_mask = (
1759                    (bboxes[:, 2] >= min_x)
1760                    & (bboxes[:, 0] <= max_x)
1761                    & (bboxes[:, 3] >= min_y)
1762                    & (bboxes[:, 1] <= max_y)
1763                )
1764                for j in np.nonzero(overlap_mask)[0]:
1765                    if j <= i:
1766                        continue
1767                    if equal_edges(
1768                        edges[i],
1769                        edges[j],
1770                        abs_tol=abs_tol,
1771                    ):
1772                        duplicate_mask[i] = True
1773                        duplicate_mask[j] = True
1774
1775            res = [
1776                edge for i, edge in enumerate(edges) if not duplicate_mask[i]
1777            ]
1778    else:
1779        unique_edges = []
1780        bbox_array = np.empty((0, 4), dtype=float)
1781
1782        for edge in edges:
1783            x1, y1 = edge[0][:2]
1784            x2, y2 = edge[1][:2]
1785            min_x = min(x1, x2)
1786            min_y = min(y1, y2)
1787            max_x = max(x1, x2)
1788            max_y = max(y1, y2)
1789
1790            duplicate = False
1791            if bbox_array.size:
1792                overlap_mask = (
1793                    (bbox_array[:, 2] >= min_x)
1794                    & (bbox_array[:, 0] <= max_x)
1795                    & (bbox_array[:, 3] >= min_y)
1796                    & (bbox_array[:, 1] <= max_y)
1797                )
1798                candidate_indices = np.nonzero(overlap_mask)[0]
1799                for candidate_index in candidate_indices:
1800                    if equal_edges(
1801                        edge,
1802                        unique_edges[candidate_index],
1803                        abs_tol=abs_tol,
1804                    ):
1805                        duplicate = True
1806                        break
1807
1808            if not duplicate:
1809                unique_edges.append(edge)
1810                bbox_row = np.array([[min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y]], dtype=float)
1811                if bbox_array.size == 0:
1812                    bbox_array = bbox_row
1813                else:
1814                    bbox_array = np.vstack((bbox_array, bbox_row))
1815
1816        res = unique_edges
1817
1818    return res
1819
1820
1821def polygon_verts_and_bbox(
1822    poly: PolygonLike,
1823) -> tuple[Sequence[PointType], float, float, float, float]:
1824    """Return comparison vertices and an axis-aligned bounding box.
1825
1826    For a ``Group``, shared edges are removed and the largest closed
1827    outline is used. If no closed outline is found, ``all_vertices`` is
1828    used instead.
1829
1830    Args:
1831        poly (PolygonLike): A ``Shape``, a ``Group``, or vertex sequence.
1832
1833    Returns:
1834        tuple: ``(vertices, min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y)``.
1835
1836    Examples:
1837        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1838        >>> verts, min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y = sg.polygon_verts_and_bbox(
1839        ... [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
1840        ... )
1841        >>> verts
1842        [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
1843        >>> (min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y)
1844        (0, 0, 40, 40)
1845"""
1846    from ...group.batch import Group
1847    from ...shapes.shape import Shape
1848
1849    if isinstance(poly, Group):
1850        sw = poly.b_box.southwest
1851        ne = poly.b_box.northeast
1852        min_x, min_y = sw[0], sw[1]
1853        max_x, max_y = ne[0], ne[1]
1854        boundary_edges = remove_duplicate_edges(poly.all_edges, keep_one=False)
1855        merged = Group([Shape(edge) for edge in boundary_edges]).merge_shapes()
1856        verts = []
1857        largest_area = -1
1858        for shape in merged:
1859            if (
1860                isinstance(shape, Shape)
1861                and shape.closed
1862                and shape.area > largest_area
1863            ):
1864                largest_area = shape.area
1865                verts = list(shape.vertices)
1866        if not verts:
1867            verts = poly.all_vertices
1868    elif isinstance(poly, Shape):
1869        verts = list(poly.vertices)
1870        sw = poly.b_box.southwest
1871        ne = poly.b_box.northeast
1872        min_x, min_y = sw[0], sw[1]
1873        max_x, max_y = ne[0], ne[1]
1874    else:
1875        verts = list(poly)
1876        xs = [p[0] for p in verts]
1877        ys = [p[1] for p in verts]
1878        min_x, min_y = min(xs), min(ys)
1879        max_x, max_y = max(xs), max(ys)
1880
1881    return verts, min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y
1882
1883
1884def remove_duplicate_polygons(
1885    polygons: Sequence[PolygonLike],
1886    mirror: bool = True,
1887    keep_one: bool = True,
1888) -> list[PolygonLike]:
1889    """Return polygons with congruent duplicates removed.
1890
1891    Polygons are grouped by vertex count. Only polygons whose shortest
1892    edge lengths match are compared with :func:`congruent_polygons`.
1893
1894    Args:
1895        polygons (Sequence[PolygonLike]): ``Shape`` objects or vertex
1896            sequences. Groups are not accepted.
1897        mirror (bool): If True, treat reflections as duplicates.
1898        keep_one (bool): If True, keep the first of each congruent class.
1899            If False, drop every polygon that has a congruent partner.
1900
1901    Returns:
1902        list[PolygonLike]: Selected polygon objects from ``polygons``.
1903
1904    Examples:
1905        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1906        >>> square = [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
1907        >>> same = [(40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40), (0, 0)]
1908        >>> tri = [(0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 80)]
1909        >>> sg.remove_duplicate_polygons([square, same, tri])
1910        [[(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], [(0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 80)]]
1911        >>> sg.remove_duplicate_polygons([square, same], keep_one=False)
1912        []
1913"""
1914    abs_tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
1915    entries = []
1916    by_n: dict[int, list[int]] = defaultdict(list)
1917
1918    for i, poly in enumerate(polygons):
1919        verts = polygon_vertices(poly)
1920        turns = rotate_turns_to_min_edge(polygon_turns(verts))
1921        start_len = turns[0] if turns else 0.0
1922        entries.append(
1923            {
1924                "poly": poly,
1925                "turns": turns,
1926                "start_len": start_len,
1927            }
1928        )
1929        by_n[len(verts)].append(i)
1930
1931    def _same_start_len(i: int, j: int) -> bool:
1932        return isclose(
1933            entries[i]["start_len"],
1934            entries[j]["start_len"],
1935            rel_tol=0.0,
1936            abs_tol=abs_tol,
1937        )
1938
1939    def _are_congruent(i: int, j: int) -> bool:
1940        if not _same_start_len(i, j):
1941            return False
1942        return congruent_polygons(
1943            entries[i]["poly"],
1944            entries[j]["poly"],
1945            mirror=mirror,
1946        )
1947
1948    n = len(polygons)
1949    if n == 0:
1950        return []
1951
1952    if keep_one:
1953        keep = [True] * n
1954        for indices in by_n.values():
1955            kept_in_group: list[int] = []
1956            for i in indices:
1957                if any(_are_congruent(i, j) for j in kept_in_group):
1958                    keep[i] = False
1959                else:
1960                    kept_in_group.append(i)
1961        res = [polygons[i] for i in range(n) if keep[i]]
1962    else:
1963        has_duplicate = [False] * n
1964        for indices in by_n.values():
1965            for a, i in enumerate(indices):
1966                for j in indices[a + 1 :]:
1967                    if _are_congruent(i, j):
1968                        has_duplicate[i] = True
1969                        has_duplicate[j] = True
1970        res = [polygons[i] for i in range(n) if not has_duplicate[i]]
1971
1972    return res
1973
1974
1975def symmetric_difference(
1976    shapes: Group, length_bound: int = 10
1977) -> tuple[Sequence[Shape], Shape]:
1978    """Return the filled faces of the symmetric difference of overlapping shapes.
1979
1980    This calls :func:`get_partitions` and :func:`set_fills`.
1981
1982    Args:
1983        shapes (Group): Overlapping polygon shapes.
1984        length_bound (int): Maximum cycle length for face enumeration.
1985            Defaults to 10.
1986
1987    Returns:
1988        tuple[Sequence[Shape], Shape]: Filled partitions and their union
1989        outline.
1990
1991    Examples:
1992        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1993        >>> square = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1994        >>> group = sg.Group([square])
1995        >>> square.closed
1996        True
1997"""
1998    partitions, d_edge_part, union = get_partitions(shapes, length_bound)
1999    set_fills(partitions, d_edge_part)
2000    print(
2001        f"* Largest partition that can be computed with length_bound = {length_bound}."
2002    )
2003    return partitions, union
2004

2006def in_polygon(
2007    point: PointType,
2008    polygon_vertices: Sequence[PointType],
2009    exclude_border: bool = False,
2010) -> bool:
2011    """Return whether a point lies inside a polygon.
2012
2013    Uses the winding number. A point on an edge is inside unless
2014    ``exclude_border`` is True.
2015
2016    Args:
2017        point (PointType): Point ``(x, y)`` to test.
2018        polygon_vertices (Sequence[PointType]): Ordered polygon vertices.
2019        exclude_border (bool): If True, points on an edge return False.
2020            Defaults to False.
2021
2022    Returns:
2023        bool: True if inside, else False.
2024
2025    Examples:
2026        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2027        >>> square = [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
2028        >>> sg.in_polygon((0.5, 0.5), square)
2029        True
2030        >>> sg.in_polygon((0.5, 0), square)
2031        True
2032        >>> sg.in_polygon((0.5, 0), square, exclude_border=True)
2033        False
2034        >>> sg.in_polygon((80, 80), square)
2035        False
2036"""
2037    _, y = point[:2]
2038    n_winding = 0  # Initialize the winding number
2039
2040    n = len(polygon_vertices)
2041    for i_ in range(n):
2042        p1 = polygon_vertices[i_]
2043        p2 = polygon_vertices[(i_ + 1) % n]  # Connect last vertex to first
2044        _, y1 = p1
2045        _, y2 = p2
2046        if point_on_line_segment(point, [p1, p2]):
2047            return not exclude_border
2048        if y1 <= y:  # Start y <= P.y
2049            if y2 > y and left3(p1, p2, point):  # An upward crossing
2050                n_winding += 1  # P left of edge
2051        elif y2 <= y and not left3(p1, p2, point):  # A downward crossing
2052            n_winding -= 1  # P right of edge
2053
2054    return n_winding != 0
2055

2057def double_offset_lines(
2058    line: LineType, offset: float = 1
2059) -> tuple[LineType, LineType]:
2060    """Return the two lines offset on either side of a segment.
2061
2062    Args:
2063        line (LineType): Input segment.
2064        offset (float): Offset distance. Defaults to 1.
2065
2066    Returns:
2067        tuple[LineType, LineType]: The positive-offset line and the
2068        negative-offset line.
2069
2070    Examples:
2071        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2072        >>> sg.double_offset_lines(((0, 0), (80, 0)), 1)
2073        ([[0.0, 1.0], [80.0, 1.0]], [[0.0, -1.0], [80.0, -1.0]])
2074"""
2075    line1 = offset_line(line, offset)
2076    line2 = offset_line(line, -offset)
2077
2078    return line1, line2

2081def double_offset_polylines(
2082    lines: Sequence[PointType],
2083    offset: float = 1,
2084    rel_tol: float | None = None,
2085    abs_tol: float | None = None,
2086) -> Sequence[Sequence[PointType]]:
2087    """Return both offset polylines of an open chain of points.
2088
2089    Args:
2090        lines (Sequence[PointType]): Polyline vertices.
2091        offset (float): Offset distance. Defaults to 1.
2092        rel_tol (float | None): Relative stitch tolerance. Defaults to
2093            ``runtime_defaults["rel_tol"]``.
2094        abs_tol (float | None): Absolute stitch tolerance. Defaults to
2095            ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
2096
2097    Returns:
2098        list: ``[positive_offset, negative_offset]``.
2099
2100    Examples:
2101        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2102        >>> sg.double_offset_polylines([(0, 0), (80, 0), (80, 80)], 1)
2103        [[[0.0, 1.0], (79.0, 1.0), [79.0, 80.0]], [[0.0, -1.0], (81.0, -1.0), [81.0, 80.0]]]
2104"""
2105    rel_tol, abs_tol = get_defaults(["rel_tol", "abs_tol"], [rel_tol, abs_tol])
2106    lines1 = []
2107    lines2 = []
2108    for i, point in enumerate(lines[:-1]):
2109        line = [point, lines[i + 1]]
2110        line1, line2 = double_offset_lines(line, offset)
2111        lines1.append(line1)
2112        lines2.append(line2)
2113    lines1 = stitch(lines1, closed=False)
2114    lines2 = stitch(lines2, closed=False)
2115    return [lines1, lines2]

2118def polygon_cg(points: Sequence[PointType]) -> PointType | None:
2119    """Return the area center of a polygon.
2120
2121    This is the center of gravity of the filled polygon, not the average
2122    of the vertices. A zero-area ring returns ``None``.
2123
2124    Args:
2125        points (Sequence[PointType]): Vertices in walk order.
2126
2127    Returns:
2128        PointType | None: Area center, or ``None`` if the area is zero.
2129
2130    Examples:
2131        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2132        >>> sg.polygon_cg([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)])
2133        [20.0, 20.0]
2134        >>> sg.polygon_cg([(0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 80)])
2135        [26.666666666666668, 26.666666666666668]
2136        >>> sg.polygon_cg([(0, 0), (40, 0), (80, 0)]) is None
2137        True
2138"""
2139    cx = cy = 0
2140    n_points = len(points)
2141    for i in range(n_points):
2142        x = points[i][0]
2143        y = points[i][1]
2144        xnext = points[(i + 1) % n_points][0]
2145        ynext = points[(i + 1) % n_points][1]
2146
2147        temp = x * ynext - xnext * y
2148        cx += (x + xnext) * temp
2149        cy += (y + ynext) * temp
2150    area_ = polygon_area(points)
2151    denom = area_ * 6
2152    if denom:
2153        res = [cx / denom, cy / denom]
2154    else:
2155        res = None
2156    return res
2157
2158
2159def offset_polygon(
2160    polygon: Sequence[PointType],
2161    offset: float = -1,
2162    abs_tol: float | None = None,
2163) -> Sequence[PointType]:
2164    """Return a closed polygon offset from ``polygon``.
2165
2166    Positive ``offset`` expands outward; negative deflates. The default
2167    ``-1`` therefore shrinks the ring by 1.
2168
2169    Args:
2170        polygon (Sequence[PointType]): Polygon vertices.
2171        offset (float): Offset distance. Defaults to -1.
2172        abs_tol (float | None): Distance used to decide whether the ring
2173            is already closed. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
2174
2175    Returns:
2176        Sequence[PointType]: Closed offset ring.
2177
2178    Examples:
2179        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2180        >>> sg.offset_polygon([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], 0.5)
2181        [(-0.5, -0.5), (40.5, -0.5), (40.5, 40.5), (-0.5, 40.5), (-0.5, -0.5)]
2182"""
2183    if abs_tol is None:
2184        abs_tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
2185    polygon = list(polygon[:])
2186    abs_tol2 = abs_tol * abs_tol
2187    if not right_handed(polygon):
2188        polygon.reverse()
2189    if not close_points_square(polygon[0], polygon[-1], dist2=abs_tol2):
2190        polygon.append(polygon[0])
2191    poly = []
2192    for i, point in enumerate(polygon[:-1]):
2193        line = [point, polygon[i + 1]]
2194        offset_edge = offset_line(line, -offset)
2195        poly.append(offset_edge)
2196
2197    poly = stitch(poly, closed=True)
2198    return poly
2199
2200
2201def double_offset_polygons(
2202    polygon: Sequence[PointType],
2203    offset: float = 1,
2204    abs_tol: float | None = None,
2205    **kwargs: Any,
2206) -> Sequence[Sequence[PointType]]:
2207    """Return both offset polygons of a vertex ring.
2208
2209    Args:
2210        polygon (Sequence[PointType]): Polygon vertices. An unclosed ring
2211            is treated as closed, and a clockwise ring is reversed for
2212            the offset calculation.
2213        offset (float): Offset distance. Defaults to 1.
2214        abs_tol (float | None): Distance used to decide whether the ring
2215            is already closed. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
2216        **kwargs (Any): If ``canvas`` is a canvas, both offsets are drawn.
2217
2218    Returns:
2219        list: ``[positive_offset, negative_offset]``.
2220
2221    Examples:
2222        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2223        >>> raw = [(0, 0), (80, 0), (80, 40)]
2224        >>> offsets = sg.double_offset_polygons(raw, 0.5)
2225        >>> raw
2226        [(0, 0), (80, 0), (80, 40)]
2227        >>> offsets[0]
2228        [(2.1180339887498945, 0.5), (79.5, 0.5), (79.5, 39.19098300562505), (2.1180339887498945, 0.5)]
2229        >>> offsets[1]
2230        [(-2.118033988749895, -0.5), (80.5, -0.5), (80.5, 40.80901699437495), (-2.118033988749895, -0.5)]
2231"""
2232    if abs_tol is None:
2233        abs_tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
2234    abs_tol2 = abs_tol * abs_tol
2235
2236    ring = list(polygon)
2237    if not close_points_square(ring[0], ring[-1], dist2=abs_tol2):
2238        ring.append(ring[0])
2239
2240    if not right_handed(ring):
2241        ring.reverse()
2242    poly1 = []
2243    poly2 = []
2244    for i, point in enumerate(ring[:-1]):
2245        line = [point, ring[i + 1]]
2246        line1, line2 = double_offset_lines(line, offset)
2247        poly1.append(line1)
2248        poly2.append(line2)
2249    poly1 = stitch(poly1)
2250    poly2 = stitch(poly2)
2251    if "canvas" in kwargs:
2252        canvas = kwargs["canvas"]
2253        if canvas:
2254            canvas.new_page()
2255            closed = close_points_square(poly1[0], poly1[-1])
2256            canvas.draw(_shape(poly1, closed=closed), fill=False)
2257            closed = close_points_square(poly2[0], poly2[-1])
2258            canvas.draw(_shape(poly2, closed=closed), fill=False)
2259    return [poly1, poly2]
2260

2262def offset_polygon_points(
2263    polygon: Sequence[PointType],
2264    offset: float = 1,
2265    abs_tol: float | None = None,
2266) -> Sequence[PointType]:
2267    """Return a stitched offset polygon.
2268
2269    Positive ``offset`` expands outward; negative deflates. Same sign
2270    convention as ``offset_polygon`` and ``inflate``.
2271
2272    Args:
2273        polygon (Sequence[PointType]): Polygon vertices.
2274        offset (float): Offset distance. Defaults to 1.
2275        abs_tol (float | None): Distance used to decide whether the ring
2276            is already closed. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
2277
2278    Returns:
2279        Sequence[PointType]: Offset ring. A clockwise result is reversed.
2280
2281    Examples:
2282        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2283        >>> sg.offset_polygon_points([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], 0.5)
2284        [(-0.5, -0.5), (40.5, -0.5), (40.5, 40.5), (-0.5, 40.5), (-0.5, -0.5)]
2285"""
2286    return offset_polygon(polygon, offset, abs_tol)

2289def polyline_length(
2290    polygon: Sequence[PointType],
2291    closed: bool = False,
2292    abs_tol: float | None = None,
2293) -> float:
2294    """Return the length of a polyline, or the perimeter if it is closed.
2295
2296    Args:
2297        polygon (Sequence[PointType]): Vertices in order.
2298        closed (bool): If True, include the closing edge when it is missing.
2299            Defaults to False.
2300        abs_tol (float | None): Distance used to decide whether the ring
2301            is already closed. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
2302
2303    Returns:
2304        float: Path length.
2305
2306    Examples:
2307        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2308        >>> sg.polyline_length([(0, 0), (60, 0), (60, 80)])
2309        140.0
2310        >>> sg.polyline_length([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
2311        160.0
2312"""
2313    if abs_tol is None:
2314        abs_tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
2315    abs_tol2 = abs_tol * abs_tol
2316    polygon = list(polygon)
2317    if closed and not close_points_square(
2318        polygon[0], polygon[-1], dist2=abs_tol2
2319    ):
2320        polygon.append(polygon[0])
2321    perimeter = 0
2322    for i, point in enumerate(polygon[:-1]):
2323        perimeter += distance(point, polygon[i + 1])
2324    return perimeter

def polygon_area( polygon: Sequence[Sequence[float]], abs_tol: float | None = None) -> float: 
258def polygon_area(
259    polygon: Sequence[PointType], abs_tol: float | None = None
260) -> float:
261    """Return the signed area of a polygon.
262
263    A counter-clockwise walk is positive. A clockwise walk is negative.
264    An unclosed ring is closed for the calculation only.
265
266    Args:
267        polygon (Sequence[PointType]): Vertices in walk order.
268        abs_tol (float | None): Distance used to decide whether the ring
269            is already closed. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
270
271    Returns:
272        float: Signed area.
273
274    Examples:
275        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
276        >>> sg.polygon_area([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)])
277        1600.0
278        >>> sg.polygon_area([(0, 0), (0, 40), (40, 40), (40, 0)])
279        -1600.0
280        >>> sg.polygon_area([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40), (0, 0)])
281        1600.0
282"""
283    if abs_tol is None:
284        abs_tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
285    abs_tol2 = abs_tol * abs_tol
286    if not close_points_square(polygon[0], polygon[-1], dist2=abs_tol2):
287        polygon = list(polygon[:])
288        polygon.append(polygon[0])
289    area_ = 0
290    for i, point in enumerate(polygon[:-1]):
291        x1, y1 = point[:2]
292        x2, y2 = polygon[i + 1][:2]
293        area_ += x1 * y2 - x2 * y1
294
295    return area_ / 2

Return the signed area of a polygon.

A counter-clockwise walk is positive. A clockwise walk is negative. An unclosed ring is closed for the calculation only.

Arguments:
  • polygon (Sequence[PointType]): Vertices in walk order.
  • abs_tol (float | None): Distance used to decide whether the ring is already closed. Defaults to runtime_defaults["abs_tol"].
Returns:

float: Signed area.

Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> sg.polygon_area([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)])
1600.0
>>> sg.polygon_area([(0, 0), (0, 40), (40, 40), (40, 0)])
-1600.0
>>> sg.polygon_area([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40), (0, 0)])
1600.0
def ccw_positive_vertices(vertices: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> list[tuple[float, float]]: 
298def ccw_positive_vertices(
299    vertices: Sequence[PointType],
300) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
301    """Return a counter-clockwise copy of ``vertices``.
302
303    A clockwise walk is reversed so the signed area is positive.
304
305    Args:
306        vertices (Sequence[PointType]): Polygon vertices in order.
307
308    Returns:
309        list[tuple[float, float]]: Counter-clockwise vertex copy.
310
311    Examples:
312        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
313        >>> sg.ccw_positive_vertices([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40)])
314        [(0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0)]
315        >>> sg.ccw_positive_vertices([(0, 0), (0, 40), (40, 0)])
316        [(40.0, 0.0), (0.0, 40.0), (0.0, 0.0)]
317"""
318    verts = [(float(x), float(y)) for x, y in vertices]
319    if polygon_area(verts) < 0:
320        verts = list(reversed(verts))
321
322    return verts
