def point_inside_polygon( p: Sequence[float], poly: Sequence[Sequence[float]], eps: float = 1e-05) -> bool: 
625def point_inside_polygon(
626    p: PointType, poly: Sequence[PointType], eps: float = 1e-5
627) -> bool:
628    """Return True only if ``p`` is strictly inside ``poly``.
629
630    Points on the boundary return False.
631
632    Args:
633        p (PointType): Query point ``(x, y)``.
634        poly (Sequence[PointType]): Ordered polygon vertices.
635        eps (float): Tolerance for on-segment tests. Defaults to ``1e-5``.
636
637    Returns:
638        bool: True if strictly inside; False on the boundary or outside.
639
640    Examples:
641        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
642        >>> square = [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
643        >>> sg.point_inside_polygon((0.5, 0.5), square)
644        True
645        >>> sg.point_inside_polygon((0.5, 0), square)
646        False
647        >>> sg.point_inside_polygon((80, 80), square)
648        False
649"""
650    x, y = p
651    n = len(poly)
652
653    # boundary check
654    for i in range(n):
655        a = poly[i]
656        b = poly[(i + 1) % n]
657        if on_segment(a, b, p, eps=eps):
658            return False
659
660    inside = False
661    for i in range(n):
662        a = poly[i]
663        b = poly[(i + 1) % n]
664        ax, ay = a
665        bx, by = b
666
667        # edge straddles horizontal ray?
668        if (ay > y) != (by > y):
669            # x intersection
670            x_int = (bx - ax) * (y - ay) / (by - ay) + ax
671            if x_int > x + eps:
672                inside = not inside
673    return inside

Return True only if p is strictly inside poly.

Points on the boundary return False.

Arguments:
  • p (PointType): Query point (x, y).
  • poly (Sequence[PointType]): Ordered polygon vertices.
  • eps (float): Tolerance for on-segment tests. Defaults to 1e-5.
Returns:

bool: True if strictly inside; False on the boundary or outside.

Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> square = [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
>>> sg.point_inside_polygon((0.5, 0.5), square)
True
>>> sg.point_inside_polygon((0.5, 0), square)
False
>>> sg.point_inside_polygon((80, 80), square)
False
def polygons_union( shapes: Sequence[simetri.shapes.shape.Shape], all_segments: Sequence[Sequence[Sequence]], all_midpoints: Sequence[Sequence[float]], min_seg_len: float = 0.001) -> tuple[simetri.shapes.shape.Shape, simetri.group.batch.Group]: 
676def polygons_union(
677    shapes: Sequence[Shape],
678    all_segments: Sequence[LineType],
679    all_midpoints: Sequence[PointType],
680    min_seg_len: float = 0.001,
681) -> tuple[Shape, Group]:
682    """Return the union boundary of polygon shapes from a segment arrangement.
683
684    A single shape is returned unchanged, with an empty hole group.
685    Shared interior edges are dropped. The midpoint of a kept segment
686    lies in exactly one input polygon.
687
688    Args:
689        shapes (Sequence[Shape]): Input polygon shapes.
690        all_segments (Sequence[LineType]): Arrangement segments.
691        all_midpoints (Sequence[PointType]): Midpoints parallel to
692            ``all_segments``.
693        min_seg_len (float): Drop segments shorter than this. Defaults
694            to ``0.001``.
695
696    Returns:
697        tuple[Shape, Group]: Outer union boundary and a group of holes.
698
699    Raises:
700        ValueError: If ``shapes`` is empty.
701
702    Examples:
703        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
704        >>> square = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
705        >>> outer, holes = sg.polygons_union([square], [], [])
706        >>> [tuple(round(c, 6) for c in p[:2]) for p in outer.vertices]
707        [(0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0)]
708        >>> holes
709        Group()
710        >>> sg.polygons_union([], [], [])
711        Traceback (most recent call last):
712        ...
713        ValueError: polygons_union requires at least one polygon
714"""
715    if len(shapes) == 0:
716        raise ValueError("polygons_union requires at least one polygon")
717    if len(shapes) == 1:
718        return shapes[0], _group([])
719
720    shape_vertices = [shape.vertices for shape in shapes]
721    counts = _segment_containment_counts(all_midpoints, shape_vertices)
722
723    # Keep arrangement segments whose midpoint lies in exactly one input polygon.
724    # Shared interior edges (count >= 2) and exterior void edges (count == 0)
725    # are dropped; count == 1 is the union-boundary (XOR) rule.
726    union_segments = []
727    for segment, _, count in zip(all_segments, all_midpoints, counts):
728        if distance(*segment) < min_seg_len:
729            continue
730        if count == 1:
731            union_segments.append(segment)
732
733    merged = _group(
734        [_shape(segment) for segment in union_segments]
735    ).merge_shapes()
736    outer = merged[0]
737    holes = [
738        part
739        for part in merged[1:]
740        if point_inside_polygon(part[-1], outer.vertices)
741    ]
742    return outer, _group(holes)

Return the union boundary of polygon shapes from a segment arrangement.

A single shape is returned unchanged, with an empty hole group. Shared interior edges are dropped. The midpoint of a kept segment lies in exactly one input polygon.

Arguments:
  • shapes (Sequence[Shape]): Input polygon shapes.
  • all_segments (Sequence[LineType]): Arrangement segments.
  • all_midpoints (Sequence[PointType]): Midpoints parallel to all_segments.
  • min_seg_len (float): Drop segments shorter than this. Defaults to 0.001.
Returns:

tuple[Shape, Group]: Outer union boundary and a group of holes.

Raises:
  • ValueError: If shapes is empty.
Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> square = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
>>> outer, holes = sg.polygons_union([square], [], [])
>>> [tuple(round(c, 6) for c in p[:2]) for p in outer.vertices]
[(0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0)]
>>> holes
Group()
>>> sg.polygons_union([], [], [])
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
ValueError: polygons_union requires at least one polygon
def all_close_points( points: Sequence[Sequence[float]], abs_tol: float | None = None, with_dist: bool = False) -> tuple[dict[int, Sequence[int]], Sequence[tuple[int, int] | tuple[int, int, float]]]: 
745def all_close_points(
746    points: Sequence[Sequence[float]],
747    abs_tol: float | None = None,
748    with_dist: bool = False,
749) -> tuple[
750    dict[int, Sequence[int]],
751    Sequence[tuple[int, int] | tuple[int, int, float]],
752]:
753    """Return close point ids, and the pairs that produced them.
754
755    Each input row is ``[x, y, id]``. Nearby points are linked in both
756    directions.
757
758    Args:
759        points (Sequence[Sequence[float]]): Rows ``[x, y, id]``.
760        abs_tol (float | None): Distance tolerance. Defaults to
761            ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
762        with_dist (bool): If True, each pair is ``(id1, id2, distance)``.
763            Defaults to False.
764
765    Returns:
766        tuple: ``({id: [nearby ids], ...}, pairs)``. Ids with no neighbor
767        are omitted from the dictionary.
768
769    Examples:
770        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
771        >>> rows = [[0, 0, 1], [0.01, 0, 2], [5, 5, 3]]
772        >>> sg.all_close_points(rows, abs_tol=0.05)
773        ({1: [2], 2: [1]}, [(1, 2)])
774        >>> links, pairs = sg.all_close_points(rows, abs_tol=0.05, with_dist=True)
775        >>> links
776        {1: [2], 2: [1]}
777        >>> round(pairs[0][2], 2)
778        0.01
779"""
780    if abs_tol is None:
781        abs_tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
782    point_arr = np.array(
783        points, dtype=np.float32
784    )  # points array [[x1, y1, id1], ...]]
785    n_rows = len(points)
786    point_arr = point_arr[point_arr[:, 0].argsort()]  # sort by x values in the
787    # first column
788    xmin = point_arr[:, 0] - abs_tol * 2
789    xmin = xmin.reshape(n_rows, 1)
790    xmax = point_arr[:, 0] + abs_tol * 2
791    xmax = xmax.reshape(n_rows, 1)
792    point_arr = np.concatenate(
793        (point_arr, xmin, xmax), 1
794    )  # [x, y, id, xmin, xmax]
795
796    i_id, i_xmin, i_xmax = 2, 3, 4  # column indices
797    d_connections = {}
798    for i in range(n_rows):
799        d_connections[int(point_arr[i, 2])] = []
800    pairs = []
801    abs_tol2 = abs_tol * abs_tol
802    for i in range(n_rows):
803        x, y, id1, sl_xmin, sl_xmax = point_arr[i, :]
804        id1 = int(id1)
805        point = (x, y)
806        start = i + 1
807        candidates = point_arr[start:, :][
808            (
809                (point_arr[start:, i_xmax] >= sl_xmin)
810                & (point_arr[start:, i_xmin] <= sl_xmax)
811            )
812        ]
813        for cand in candidates:
814            id2 = int(cand[i_id])
815            point2 = cand[:2]
816            if close_points_square(point, point2, dist2=abs_tol2):
817                d_connections[id1].append(id2)
818                d_connections[id2].append(id1)
819                if with_dist:
820                    pairs.append((id1, id2, distance(point, point2)))
821                else:
822                    pairs.append((id1, id2))
823    res = {node_id: connections for node_id, connections in d_connections.items() if connections}
824    return res, pairs

Return close point ids, and the pairs that produced them.

Each input row is [x, y, id]. Nearby points are linked in both directions.

Arguments:
  • points (Sequence[Sequence[float]]): Rows [x, y, id].
  • abs_tol (float | None): Distance tolerance. Defaults to runtime_defaults["abs_tol"].
  • with_dist (bool): If True, each pair is (id1, id2, distance). Defaults to False.
Returns:

tuple: ({id: [nearby ids], ...}, pairs). Ids with no neighbor are omitted from the dictionary.

Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> rows = [[0, 0, 1], [0.01, 0, 2], [5, 5, 3]]
>>> sg.all_close_points(rows, abs_tol=0.05)
({1: [2], 2: [1]}, [(1, 2)])
>>> links, pairs = sg.all_close_points(rows, abs_tol=0.05, with_dist=True)
>>> links
{1: [2], 2: [1]}
>>> round(pairs[0][2], 2)
0.01
def node_dictionaries( coords: Sequence[Sequence[float]], abs_tol: float, debug: bool = False) -> tuple[dict[int, tuple[float, ...]], dict[tuple[float, ...], int], dict[tuple[float, ...], Sequence[float]]]: 
827def node_dictionaries(
828    coords: Sequence[PointType],
829    abs_tol: float,
830    debug: bool = False,
831) -> tuple[
832    dict[int, tuple[float, ...]],
833    dict[tuple[float, ...], int],
834    dict[tuple[float, ...], PointType],
835]:
836    """Return node maps for coordinates that fall within ``abs_tol``.
837
838    Nearby coordinates share one node id. The third map keeps the original
839    coordinate for each rounded key.
840
841    Args:
842        coords (Sequence[PointType]): Vertices to index.
843        abs_tol (float): Distance used to merge nearby coordinates.
844        debug (bool): If True, print the closest unmerged pair.
845            Defaults to False.
846
847    Returns:
848        tuple: ``(node_to_coord, coord_to_node, rounded_to_original)``.
849
850    Examples:
851        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
852        >>> nodes, coord_node, rounded = sg.node_dictionaries(
853        ... [(0, 0), (0.01, 0), (20, 20)], 0.05
854        ... )
855        >>> nodes
856        {0: (0, 0), 1: (20, 20)}
857        >>> coord_node[(0, 0)] == coord_node[(0.01, 0)]
858        True
859        >>> rounded[(20, 20)]
860        (20, 20)
861"""
862    n_round = max(0, ceil(log10(sqrt(2) / abs_tol)))
863    d_rounded_coord = {}
864    rounded = []
865    for coord in coords:
866        val = tuple(round_point(coord, n_round))
867        rounded.append(val)
868        d_rounded_coord[val] = coord
869
870    rounded_coords = list(set(rounded))
871    rounded_coords.sort()
872    rounded_coords.sort(key=lambda point: point[1])
873
874    indexed_coordinates = [
875        (*coordinate[:2], index)
876        for index, coordinate in enumerate(rounded_coords)
877    ]
878    _, close_pairs = all_close_points(indexed_coordinates, abs_tol=abs_tol)
879    parent = list(range(len(rounded_coords)))
880    for first_index, second_index in close_pairs:
881        first_root = first_index
882        while parent[first_root] != first_root:
883            first_root = parent[first_root]
884        second_root = second_index
885        while parent[second_root] != second_root:
886            second_root = parent[second_root]
887        if first_root != second_root:
888            parent[second_root] = first_root
889
890    d_node_coord = {}
891    d_coord_node = {}
892
893    root_node = {}
894    for coordinate_index, coordinate in enumerate(rounded_coords):
895        root = coordinate_index
896        while parent[root] != root:
897            root = parent[root]
898        if root not in root_node:
899            node = len(root_node)
900            root_node[root] = node
901            d_node_coord[node] = rounded_coords[root]
902        d_coord_node[coordinate] = root_node[root]
903
904    if debug:
905        closest_distance = None
906        closest_points = None
907        for first_point, second_point in combinations(coords, 2):
908            first_coordinate = tuple(round_point(first_point, n_round))
909            second_coordinate = tuple(round_point(second_point, n_round))
910            if (
911                d_coord_node[first_coordinate]
912                == d_coord_node[second_coordinate]
913            ):
914                continue
915            point_distance = distance(first_point, second_point)
916            if closest_distance is None or point_distance < closest_distance:
917                closest_distance = point_distance
918                closest_points = (first_point[:2], second_point[:2])
919        print(
920            "Node diagnostics: "
921            f"abs_tol={abs_tol}; automatic n_round={n_round}; "
922            f"nodes={len(d_node_coord)}"
923        )
924        print(
925            "  Closest unmerged point distance: "
926            f"{closest_distance}; points={closest_points}"
927        )
928
929    return (d_node_coord, d_coord_node, d_rounded_coord)

Return node maps for coordinates that fall within abs_tol.

Nearby coordinates share one node id. The third map keeps the original coordinate for each rounded key.

Arguments:
  • coords (Sequence[PointType]): Vertices to index.
  • abs_tol (float): Distance used to merge nearby coordinates.
  • debug (bool): If True, print the closest unmerged pair. Defaults to False.
Returns:

tuple: (node_to_coord, coord_to_node, rounded_to_original).

Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> nodes, coord_node, rounded = sg.node_dictionaries(
... [(0, 0), (0.01, 0), (20, 20)], 0.05
... )
>>> nodes
{0: (0, 0), 1: (20, 20)}
>>> coord_node[(0, 0)] == coord_node[(0.01, 0)]
True
>>> rounded[(20, 20)]
(20, 20)
def segment_cycles( segments: Sequence[Sequence[Sequence]], length_bound: int = 10, cycle_basis: bool = False, abs_tol: float | None = None) -> tuple[list, list]: 
932def segment_cycles(
933    segments: Sequence[LineType],
934    length_bound: int = 10,
935    cycle_basis: bool = False,
936    abs_tol: float | None = None,
937) -> tuple[list, list]:
938    """Return closed walks formed by line segments.
939
940    Args:
941        segments (Sequence[LineType]): Segments ``[(p1, p2), ...]``.
942        length_bound (int): Maximum cycle length. Defaults to 10.
943        cycle_basis (bool): If True, use a cycle basis. Defaults to False.
944        abs_tol (float | None): Distance for merging nearby endpoints.
945            Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
946
947    Returns:
948        tuple: ``(coordinate_cycles, node_id_cycles)``.
949
950    Examples:
951        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
952        >>> square = [
953        ... ((0, 0), (40, 0)),
954        ... ((40, 0), (40, 40)),
955        ... ((40, 40), (0, 40)),
956        ... ((0, 40), (0, 0)),
957        ... ]
958        >>> coords, nodes = sg.segment_cycles(square)
959        >>> coords
960        [[(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]]
961        >>> len(nodes[0])
962        4
963"""
964    if abs_tol is None:
965        abs_tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
966    coordinates = []
967    for seg in segments:
968        coordinates.extend(seg)
969
970    d_node_coord, d_coord_node, _ = node_dictionaries(coordinates, abs_tol)
971    n_round = max(0, ceil(log10(sqrt(2) / abs_tol)))
972    g_segments = [
973        [d_coord_node[tuple(round_point(coord, n_round))] for coord in seg]
974        for seg in segments
975    ]
976
977    nx_graph = nx.Graph()
978    nx_graph.update(g_segments)
979    if cycle_basis:
980        cycles = [
981            cycle
982            for cycle in nx.cycle_basis(nx_graph)
983            if len(cycle) <= length_bound
984        ]
985    else:
986        cycles = list(nx.simple_cycles(nx_graph, length_bound=length_bound))
987    res = [[d_node_coord[node] for node in cycle] for cycle in cycles]
988
989    return res, cycles

def segments_from_points( points: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> tuple[Sequence[float], Sequence[float]] | None: 
 992def segments_from_points(
 993    points: Sequence[PointType],
 994) -> tuple[PointType, PointType] | None:
 995    """Return consecutive segments after sorting collinear points.
 996
 997    Args:
 998        points (Sequence[PointType]): Collinear points in any order.
 999
1000    Returns:
1001        list[tuple[PointType, PointType]] | None: Sorted segments, or
1002        ``None`` if fewer than two points are given.
1003
1004    Examples:
1005        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1006        >>> sg.segments_from_points([(80, 0), (0, 0), (40, 0)])
1007        [((0, 0), (40, 0)), ((40, 0), (80, 0))]
1008        >>> sg.segments_from_points([(0, 0), (40, 0)])
1009        [((0, 0), (40, 0))]
1010        >>> sg.segments_from_points([(0, 0)]) is None
1011        True
1012"""
1013    n = len(points)
1014    if n < 2:
1015        res = None
1016    elif n == 2:
1017        res = [tuple(points)]
1018    else:
1019        sorted_points = sorted(points, key=lambda p: (p[0], p[1]))
1020        segments = list(pairwise(sorted_points))
1021        res = segments
1022
1023    return res

def set_fills( partitions: Sequence[simetri.shapes.shape.Shape], d_edge_part: dict[frozenset, set[int]]) -> None: 
1026def set_fills(
1027    partitions: Sequence[Shape], d_edge_part: dict[frozenset, set[int]]
1028) -> None:
1029    """Set each partition's fill from the symmetric-difference rule.
1030
1031    An outer partition, one that owns an edge alone, is filled. Across a
1032    shared edge the neighboring fill is the opposite value.
1033
1034    Args:
1035        partitions (Sequence[Shape]): Closed partition shapes (mutated).
1036        d_edge_part (dict[frozenset, set[int]]): Edge to partition-id map.
1037
1038    Returns:
1039        None: Fills are written onto the partition objects.
1040
1041    Examples:
1042        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1043        >>> outer = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (80, 0), (80, 80), (0, 80)], closed=True)
1044        >>> edges = {frozenset(edge): {outer.id} for edge in outer.edges}
1045        >>> sg.set_fills([outer], edges)
1046        >>> outer.fill
1047        True
1048"""
1049
1050    # To start, find an edge with a single partition.
1051    # and the partition to the queue.
1052    # This is one of the outermost partitions.
1053    # Since outer partitions are always filled,
1054    # set this partition's fill property True.
1055    for edge, part in d_edge_part.items():
1056        if len(part) == 1:
1057            cur_part = d_id_obj[next(iter(part))]
1058            queue = {cur_part.id}
1059            cur_part.fill = True
1060            break
1061    # If an edge is between two partitions,
1062    # only one partition can be filled.
1063    # Alternate through all partitions.
1064    processed = set()
1065    count = 0
1066    qcount = 0
1067    while queue:
1068        count += 1
1069        cur_part = d_id_obj[queue.pop()]
1070        count += 1
1071        if cur_part.id not in processed:
1072            qcount += 1
1073            edges = [frozenset(e) for e in cur_part.edges]
1074            for edge in edges:
1075                partitions = d_edge_part[edge]
1076                if len(partitions) == 2:
1077                    part1, part2 = [d_id_obj[p] for p in partitions]
1078                    fill = not cur_part.fill
1079                    if part1 == cur_part:
1080                        part2.fill = fill
1081                    else:
1082                        part1.fill = fill
1083
1084                queue.update(set(partitions))
1085            processed.add(cur_part.id)
1086            queue.difference_update(processed)

Set each partition's fill from the symmetric-difference rule.

An outer partition, one that owns an edge alone, is filled. Across a shared edge the neighboring fill is the opposite value.

Arguments:
  • partitions (Sequence[Shape]): Closed partition shapes (mutated).
  • d_edge_part (dict[frozenset, set[int]]): Edge to partition-id map.
Returns:

None: Fills are written onto the partition objects.

Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> outer = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (80, 0), (80, 80), (0, 80)], closed=True)
>>> edges = {frozenset(edge): {outer.id} for edge in outer.edges}
>>> sg.set_fills([outer], edges)
>>> outer.fill

def any_point_inside_polygon( points: Sequence[Sequence[float]], polygon: simetri.shapes.shape.Shape | numpy.ndarray[tuple[int, ...], numpy.dtype[+_ScalarType_co]], eps: float = 1e-12) -> bool: 
1089def any_point_inside_polygon(
1090    points: Sequence[PointType],
1091    polygon: Shape | NDArray,
1092    eps: float = 1e-12,
1093) -> bool:
1094    """Return True if any point is strictly inside the polygon.
1095
1096    Boundary points are treated as outside.
1097
1098    Args:
1099        points (Sequence[PointType]): Query points ``(x, y)``.
1100        polygon (Shape | NDArray): Closed vertex ring, or a closed ``Shape``.
1101        eps (float): Tolerance for on-edge tests. Defaults to ``1e-12``.
1102
1103    Returns:
1104        bool: True if at least one point is inside and not on the boundary.
1105
1106    Examples:
1107        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1108        >>> square = [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
1109        >>> sg.any_point_inside_polygon([(80, 80), (0.2, 0.2)], square)
1110        True
1111        >>> sg.any_point_inside_polygon([(80, 80), (60, 60)], square)
1112        False
1113        >>> sg.any_point_inside_polygon([(0.5, 0)], square)
1114        False
1115"""
1116
1117    pts = np.asarray(points, dtype=float)
1118    poly = np.asarray(polygon, dtype=float)
1119
1120    px = pts[:, 0][:, None]  # (M,1)
1121    py = pts[:, 1][:, None]
1122
1123    x1 = poly[:, 0]
1124    y1 = poly[:, 1]
1125    x2 = np.roll(x1, -1)
1126    y2 = np.roll(y1, -1)
1127
1128    # -----------------------------
1129    # Boundary detection (on edge)
1130    # -----------------------------
1131    cross = (py - y1) * (x2 - x1) - (px - x1) * (y2 - y1)
1132
1133    on_seg = (
1134        (np.abs(cross) < eps)
1135        & (np.minimum(x1, x2) <= px)
1136        & (px <= np.maximum(x1, x2))
1137        & (np.minimum(y1, y2) <= py)
1138        & (py <= np.maximum(y1, y2))
1139    )
1140
1141    # Any point on boundary is NOT considered inside
1142    on_boundary = np.any(on_seg, axis=1)
1143
1144    # -----------------------------
1145    # Ray casting (interior test)
1146    # -----------------------------
1147    cond = (y1 > py) != (y2 > py)
1148    x_intersect = (x2 - x1) * (py - y1) / (y2 - y1 + 1e-15) + x1
1149
1150    inside = np.sum(cond & (px < x_intersect), axis=1) % 2 == 1
1151
1152    # Exclude boundary points from interior
1153    inside_strict = inside & (~on_boundary)
1154
1155    return np.any(inside_strict)

Return True if any point is strictly inside the polygon.

Boundary points are treated as outside.

Arguments:
  • points (Sequence[PointType]): Query points (x, y).
  • polygon (Shape | NDArray): Closed vertex ring, or a closed Shape.
  • eps (float): Tolerance for on-edge tests. Defaults to 1e-12.
Returns:

bool: True if at least one point is inside and not on the boundary.

Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> square = [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
>>> sg.any_point_inside_polygon([(80, 80), (0.2, 0.2)], square)
True
>>> sg.any_point_inside_polygon([(80, 80), (60, 60)], square)
False
>>> sg.any_point_inside_polygon([(0.5, 0)], square)
False
def get_partitions( shapes: simetri.group.batch.Group, length_bound: int = 10) -> tuple[Sequence[simetri.shapes.shape.Shape], collections.defaultdict[frozenset, set[int]], simetri.shapes.shape.Shape]: 
1158def get_partitions(
1159    shapes: Group, length_bound: int = 10
1160) -> tuple[Sequence[Shape], defaultdict[frozenset, set[int]], Shape]:
1161    """Partition overlapping shapes into face regions from their arrangement.
1162
1163    Prints cycle and hole counts while it runs.
1164
1165    Args:
1166        shapes (Group): Group whose segments define the arrangement.
1167        length_bound (int): Maximum cycle length when enumerating faces.
1168            Defaults to 10.
1169
1170    Returns:
1171        tuple: ``(partition_shapes, membership_map, merged_outline)``.
1172
1173    Examples:
1174        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1175        >>> square = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1176        >>> parts, _, outline = sg.get_partitions(sg.Group([square]))
1177        Number of total cycles with less than 10 nodes: 5
1178        Number of holes: 0
1179        Total partition-area: 1600.00, Union-area: 1600.00
1180        5 partitions.
1181        Largest* partition has 4 edges.
1182        Used 5 cycles.
1183        >>> [tuple(round(c, 6) for c in p[:2]) for p in outline.vertices]
1184        [(0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.0), (40.0, 40.0), (0.0, 40.0)]
1185"""
1186    n_edges = len(shapes.all_segments)
1187    intersections = all_intersections(
1188        shapes.all_segments, return_points_list=True
1189    )
1190    points_by_edge = defaultdict(list)
1191    for edge_id, edge in enumerate(shapes.all_segments):
1192        start_point, end_point = edge
1193        points_by_edge[edge_id].extend(
1194            (round_point(start_point), round_point(end_point))
1195        )
1196    for point, (first_edge_id, second_edge_id) in intersections:
1197        rounded_point = round_point(point)
1198        points_by_edge[first_edge_id].append(rounded_point)
1199        points_by_edge[second_edge_id].append(rounded_point)
1200
1201    all_segments = []
1202    all_midpoints = []
1203    for i in range(n_edges):
1204        points = points_by_edge[i]
1205        if len(points) >= 2:
1206            segments = segments_from_points(points)
1207            rounded_segments = [round_segment(seg, 2) for seg in segments]
1208            all_segments.extend(rounded_segments)
1209            all_midpoints.extend(
1210                midpoint(*segment) for segment in rounded_segments
1211            )
1212
1213    midpoint_array = np.unique(np.asarray(all_midpoints, dtype=float), axis=0)
1214    midpoint_order = midpoint_array[:, 0].argsort()
1215    midpoint_array = midpoint_array[midpoint_order]
1216
1217    cycles, cycles_nodes = segment_cycles(
1218        all_segments, length_bound=length_bound
1219    )
1220
1221    print(
1222        f"Number of total cycles with less than {length_bound} nodes: {len(cycles)}"
1223    )
1224    sorted_cycles = sorted(
1225        zip(cycles, cycles_nodes), key=lambda cycle_pair: len(cycle_pair[0])
1226    )
1227    cycles = [cycle_pair[0] for cycle_pair in sorted_cycles]
1228    cycles_nodes = [cycle_pair[1] for cycle_pair in sorted_cycles]
1229    union, holes = polygons_union(shapes, all_segments, all_midpoints)
1230    print(f"Number of holes: {len(holes)}")
1231    holes_area = sum([polygon_area(hole.vertices) for hole in holes])
1232    union_area = polygon_area(union.vertices) - holes_area
1233    hole_index, sorted_hole_arrays, hole_processed = _build_hole_index(holes)
1234    abs_tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
1235
1236    count = 0
1237    area = 0
1238    partitions = []
1239    d_edge_partition = defaultdict(set)
1240    done = False
1241    for poly in cycles:
1242        if done:
1243            break
1244        polygon_array = np.asarray(poly, dtype=float)
1245        polygon_min_x = polygon_array[:, 0].min()
1246        polygon_max_x = polygon_array[:, 0].max()
1247        polygon_min_y = polygon_array[:, 1].min()
1248        polygon_max_y = polygon_array[:, 1].max()
1249        midpoint_start = np.searchsorted(
1250            midpoint_array[:, 0], polygon_min_x, side="left"
1251        )
1252        midpoint_end = np.searchsorted(
1253            midpoint_array[:, 0], polygon_max_x, side="right"
1254        )
1255        candidate_midpoints = midpoint_array[midpoint_start:midpoint_end]
1256        candidate_midpoints = candidate_midpoints[
1257            (candidate_midpoints[:, 1] >= polygon_min_y)
1258            & (candidate_midpoints[:, 1] <= polygon_max_y)
1259        ]
1260        if not any_point_inside_polygon(candidate_midpoints, polygon_array):
1261            count += 1
1262            sorted_partition = sorted_polygon_xy_array(poly)
1263            candidate_hole_ids = _candidate_hole_ids(
1264                hole_index,
1265                hole_processed,
1266                polygon_min_x,
1267                polygon_min_y,
1268                polygon_max_x,
1269                polygon_max_y,
1270                abs_tol,
1271            )
1272            is_hole = False
1273            for hole_id in candidate_hole_ids:
1274                if equal_sorted_arrays(
1275                    sorted_partition,
1276                    sorted_hole_arrays[hole_id],
1277                    abs_tol,
1278                ):
1279                    is_hole = True
1280                    hole_processed[hole_id] = True
1281                    break
1282            if is_hole:
1283                continue
1284            partition = _shape(poly, closed=True)
1285            partitions.append(partition)
1286            for edge in partition.edges:
1287                d_edge_partition[frozenset(edge)].add(partition.id)
1288            poly_area = abs(
1289                polygon_area(poly)
1290            )  # Here, we are not strict about polygons' orientation
1291            area += poly_area
1292
1293            if isclose(area, union_area, rel_tol=0.001):
1294                print(
1295                    f"Total partition-area: {area:.2f}, Union-area: {union_area:.2f}"
1296                )
1297                done = True
1298
1299    print(f"{len(partitions)} partitions.")
1300    n = max((len(p) for p in partitions), default=0)
1301    print(f"Largest* partition has {n} edges.")
1302    print(f"Used {count} cycles.")
1303
1304    return partitions, d_edge_partition, union

def equal_sorted_arrays( array1: numpy.ndarray[tuple[int, ...], numpy.dtype[numpy.float64]], array2: numpy.ndarray[tuple[int, ...], numpy.dtype[numpy.float64]], abs_tol: float) -> bool: 
1307def equal_sorted_arrays(
1308    array1: NDArray[np.float64],
1309    array2: NDArray[np.float64],
1310    abs_tol: float,
1311) -> bool:
1312    """Return True if two same-shaped point arrays match within ``abs_tol``.
1313
1314    Args:
1315        array1 (NDArray[np.float64]): First ``(n, 2)`` point array.
1316        array2 (NDArray[np.float64]): Second ``(n, 2)`` point array.
1317        abs_tol (float): Maximum allowed per-point distance.
1318
1319    Returns:
1320        bool: True if every corresponding pair is within tolerance.
1321
1322    Examples:
1323        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1324        >>> square = [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
1325        >>> same = [(40, 40), (0, 40), (0, 0), (40, 0)]
1326        >>> sg.equal_sorted_arrays(
1327        ... sg.sorted_polygon_xy_array(square),
1328        ... sg.sorted_polygon_xy_array(same),
1329        ... 0.05,
1330        ... )
1331        True
1332        >>> sg.equal_sorted_arrays(
1333        ... sg.sorted_polygon_xy_array(square),
1334        ... sg.sorted_polygon_xy_array([(0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 80)]),
1335        ... 0.05,
1336        ... )
1337        False
1338"""
1339    if array1.shape != array2.shape:
1340        return False
1341    n_vertices = array1.shape[0]
1342    if n_vertices == 0:
1343        return True
1344    abs_tol2 = abs_tol * abs_tol
1345    if n_vertices <= 12:
1346        for index in range(n_vertices):
1347            dx = array1[index, 0] - array2[index, 0]
1348            dy = array1[index, 1] - array2[index, 1]
1349            if dx * dx + dy * dy > abs_tol2:
1350                return False
1351        return True
1352    delta = array1 - array2
1353
1354    return bool(np.all((delta * delta).sum(axis=1) <= abs_tol2))

Return True if two same-shaped point arrays match within abs_tol.

Returns:

def polygon_xy_array( polygon: simetri.shapes.shape.Shape | Sequence[Sequence[float]] | numpy.ndarray[tuple[int, ...], numpy.dtype[typing.Any]]) -> numpy.ndarray[tuple[int, ...], numpy.dtype[numpy.float64]]: 
1453def polygon_xy_array(
1454    polygon: Shape | Sequence[PointType] | NDArray[Any],
1455) -> NDArray[np.float64]:
1456    """Return an ``(n, 2)`` float array of polygon xy coordinates.
1457
1458    Args:
1459        polygon (Shape | Sequence[PointType] | NDArray[Any]): A ``Shape``,
1460            point sequence, or array-like.
1461
1462    Returns:
1463        NDArray[np.float64]: XY coordinates. A ``Shape`` uses
1464        ``final_coords``.
1465
1466    Examples:
1467        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1468        >>> [tuple(row) for row in sg.polygon_xy_array([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40)])]

1471        (1, 2)

1473    from simetri.shapes.shape import Shape
1474

1476        # final_coords is the cached primary_points @ xform_matrix result

1478    array = np.asarray(polygon, dtype=float)
1479    if array.ndim == 1:
1480        array = array.reshape(1, -1)
1481
1482    return array[:, :2]

1485def sorted_polygon_xy_array(
1486    polygon: Shape | Sequence[PointType] | NDArray[Any],
1487) -> NDArray[np.float64]:
1488    """Return polygon xy coordinates sorted by ``x`` then ``y``.
1489
1490    Args:

1492            point sequence, or array-like.
1493
1494    Returns:
1495        NDArray[np.float64]: Lexicographically sorted XY coordinates.
1496
1497    Examples:

1501"""
1502    array = polygon_xy_array(polygon)
1503    order = np.lexsort((array[:, 1], array[:, 0]))
1504
1505    return array[order]

def polygon_turns(vertices: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> list[float]: 
1536def polygon_turns(vertices: Sequence[PointType]) -> list[float]:
1537    """Return the signed turn sequence of a polygon.
1538
1539    For each vertex, records the outgoing edge length and the signed turn
1540    angle at the next vertex. Angles are rounded to
1541    ``runtime_defaults["turn_angle_digits"]``.
1542
1543    Args:
1544        vertices (Sequence[PointType]): Polygon vertices in walk order.
1545            The first vertex is not repeated.
1546
1547    Returns:
1548        list[float]: Alternating side lengths and turn angles.
1549
1550    Examples:
1551        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1552        >>> sg.polygon_turns([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)])
1553        [40.0, -1.57, 40.0, -1.57, 40.0, -1.57, 40.0, -1.57]
1554        >>> sg.polygon_turns([(0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 40)])
1555        [80.0, -0.46, 89.44271909999159, -1.11, 40.0, -1.57]
1556"""
1557    n = len(vertices)
1558    res = []
1559    TURN_ANGLE_DIGITS = runtime_defaults["turn_angle_digits"]
1560    for i in range(n):
1561        vert = vertices[i]
1562        next_vert = vertices[(i + 1) % n]
1563        next_seg = (next_vert, vertices[(i + 2) % n])
1564        seg = (vert, next_vert)
1565        angle = angle_between_lines3(vert, *next_seg)
1566        res.append(distance(*seg))
1567        res.append(round(angle, TURN_ANGLE_DIGITS))
1568
1569    return res

def rotate_turns_to_min_edge(turns: Sequence[float]) -> list[float]: 
1572def rotate_turns_to_min_edge(turns: Sequence[float]) -> list[float]:
1573    """Rotate a flat ``[length, angle, ...]`` cycle to start at a shortest edge.
1574
1575    Args:
1576        turns (Sequence[float]): Alternating edge lengths and turn angles.
1577
1578    Returns:
1579        list[float]: Cycle starting at the shortest edge.
1580
1581    Examples:
1582        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1583        >>> sg.rotate_turns_to_min_edge([3.0, 1.57, 1.0, 1.57, 2.0, 1.57])
1584        [1.0, 1.57, 2.0, 1.57, 3.0, 1.57]
1585        >>> sg.rotate_turns_to_min_edge([1.0])
1586        [1.0]
1587"""
1588    if len(turns) < 2:
1589        return list(turns)
1590    n_edges = len(turns) // 2
1591    min_i = min(range(n_edges), key=lambda i: turns[2 * i])
1592    start = 2 * min_i
1593    return list(turns[start:]) + list(turns[:start])

[1.0, 1.57, 2.0, 1.57, 3.0, 1.57]
>>> sg.rotate_turns_to_min_edge([1.0])
[1.0]
def congruent_polygons( polygon1: Union[simetri.shapes.shape.Shape, Sequence[Sequence[float]]], polygon2: Union[simetri.shapes.shape.Shape, Sequence[Sequence[float]]], mirror: bool = False, rel_tol: float | None = None, abs_tol: float | None = None) -> bool: 
1596def congruent_polygons(
1597    polygon1: PolygonLike,
1598    polygon2: PolygonLike,
1599    mirror: bool = False,
1600    rel_tol: float | None = None,
1601    abs_tol: float | None = None,
1602) -> bool:
1603    """Return True if ``polygon1`` and ``polygon2`` are congruent.
1604
1605    Congruence ignores translation and rotation. Signed turn sequences are
1606    compared cyclically so convex and reflex corners stay distinct.
1607
1608    Args:
1609        polygon1 (PolygonLike): First polygon as a ``Shape`` or points.
1610        polygon2 (PolygonLike): Second polygon as a ``Shape`` or points.
1611        mirror (bool): If True, a reflection also counts as congruent.
1612        rel_tol (float | None): Relative tolerance for turn comparison.
1613            Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["rel_tol"]``.
1614        abs_tol (float | None): Absolute tolerance for turn comparison.
1615            Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
1616
1617    Returns:
1618        bool: True if the polygons are congruent.
1619
1620    Examples:
1621        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1622        >>> square = [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
1623        >>> sg.congruent_polygons(square, [(40, 40), (80, 40), (80, 80), (40, 80)])
1624        True
1625        >>> sg.congruent_polygons(square, [(0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 80)])
1626        False
1627"""
1628    from ...helpers.utilities import equal_cycles
1629
1630    rel_tol, abs_tol = get_defaults(["rel_tol", "abs_tol"], [rel_tol, abs_tol])
1631    verts1 = polygon_vertices(polygon1)
1632    verts2 = polygon_vertices(polygon2)
1633    if len(verts1) != len(verts2):
1634        res = False
1635    else:
1636        poly1_turns = polygon_turns(verts1)
1637        poly2_turns = polygon_turns(verts2)
1638
1639        if mirror:
1640            if equal_cycles(poly1_turns, poly2_turns, rel_tol, abs_tol):
1641                res = True
1642            else:
1643                poly2_turns.reverse()
1644                res = equal_cycles(poly1_turns, poly2_turns, rel_tol, abs_tol)
1645        else:
1646            res = equal_cycles(poly1_turns, poly2_turns, rel_tol, abs_tol)
1647
1648    return res

Return True if polygon1 and polygon2 are congruent.

Congruence ignores translation and rotation. Signed turn sequences are compared cyclically so convex and reflex corners stay distinct.

Arguments:
  • polygon1 (PolygonLike): First polygon as a Shape or points.
  • polygon2 (PolygonLike): Second polygon as a Shape or points.
  • mirror (bool): If True, a reflection also counts as congruent.
  • rel_tol (float | None): Relative tolerance for turn comparison. Defaults to runtime_defaults["rel_tol"].
  • abs_tol (float | None): Absolute tolerance for turn comparison. Defaults to runtime_defaults["abs_tol"].
Returns:

bool: True if the polygons are congruent.

Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> square = [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
>>> sg.congruent_polygons(square, [(40, 40), (80, 40), (80, 80), (40, 80)])
True
>>> sg.congruent_polygons(square, [(0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 80)])
False

1651def equal_polygons(
1652    polygon1: PolygonLike,
1653    polygon2: PolygonLike,
1654    mirror: bool = False,
1655    rel_tol: float | None = None,
1656    abs_tol: float | None = None,
1657) -> bool:
1658    """Return True if two polygons are congruent.
1659
1660    This is an alias of :func:`congruent_polygons`.
1661
1662    Args:
1663        polygon1 (PolygonLike): First polygon.
1664        polygon2 (PolygonLike): Second polygon.
1665        mirror (bool): If True, a reflection also counts. Defaults to False.
1666        rel_tol (float | None): Relative tolerance for turn comparison.
1667            Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["rel_tol"]``.
1668        abs_tol (float | None): Absolute tolerance for turn comparison.
1669            Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
1670
1671    Returns:

1673

1680        False

def remove_duplicate_edges( edges: Sequence[Sequence[Sequence]], keep_one: bool = False) -> list[Sequence[Sequence]]: 
1713def remove_duplicate_edges(
1714    edges: Sequence[LineType],
1715    keep_one: bool = False,
1716) -> list[LineType]:
1717    """Return edges with congruent duplicates handled.
1718
1719    Candidates are filtered by axis-aligned bounding-box overlap before
1720    ``equal_edges``.
1721
1722    Args:
1723        edges (Sequence[LineType]): Segments ``(point1, point2)``.
1724        keep_one (bool): If True, keep the first copy of each congruent
1725            edge. If False, drop every edge that has a congruent duplicate.
1726
1727    Returns:
1728        list[LineType]: Selected edges.
1729
1730    Examples:
1731        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1732        >>> edges = [((0, 0), (40, 0)), ((40, 0), (0, 0)), ((0, 40), (40, 40))]
1733        >>> sg.remove_duplicate_edges(edges)
1734        [((0, 40), (40, 40))]
1735        >>> sg.remove_duplicate_edges(edges, keep_one=True)
1736        [((0, 0), (40, 0)), ((0, 40), (40, 40))]
1737"""
1738    abs_tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
1739
1740    if not keep_one:
1741        n = len(edges)
1742        if n == 0:
1743            res = []
1744        else:
1745            bboxes = np.empty((n, 4), dtype=float)
1746            for i, edge in enumerate(edges):
1747                x1, y1 = edge[0][:2]
1748                x2, y2 = edge[1][:2]
1749                bboxes[i] = [
1750                    min(x1, x2),
1751                    min(y1, y2),
1752                    max(x1, x2),
1753                    max(y1, y2),
1754                ]
1755
1756            duplicate_mask = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)
1757            for i in range(n):
1758                min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y = bboxes[i]
1759                overlap_mask = (
1760                    (bboxes[:, 2] >= min_x)
1761                    & (bboxes[:, 0] <= max_x)
1762                    & (bboxes[:, 3] >= min_y)
1763                    & (bboxes[:, 1] <= max_y)
1764                )
1765                for j in np.nonzero(overlap_mask)[0]:
1766                    if j <= i:
1767                        continue
1768                    if equal_edges(
1769                        edges[i],
1770                        edges[j],
1771                        abs_tol=abs_tol,
1772                    ):
1773                        duplicate_mask[i] = True
1774                        duplicate_mask[j] = True
1775
1776            res = [
1777                edge for i, edge in enumerate(edges) if not duplicate_mask[i]
1778            ]
1779    else:
1780        unique_edges = []
1781        bbox_array = np.empty((0, 4), dtype=float)
1782
1783        for edge in edges:
1784            x1, y1 = edge[0][:2]
1785            x2, y2 = edge[1][:2]
1786            min_x = min(x1, x2)
1787            min_y = min(y1, y2)
1788            max_x = max(x1, x2)
1789            max_y = max(y1, y2)
1790
1791            duplicate = False
1792            if bbox_array.size:
1793                overlap_mask = (
1794                    (bbox_array[:, 2] >= min_x)
1795                    & (bbox_array[:, 0] <= max_x)
1796                    & (bbox_array[:, 3] >= min_y)
1797                    & (bbox_array[:, 1] <= max_y)
1798                )
1799                candidate_indices = np.nonzero(overlap_mask)[0]
1800                for candidate_index in candidate_indices:
1801                    if equal_edges(
1802                        edge,
1803                        unique_edges[candidate_index],
1804                        abs_tol=abs_tol,
1805                    ):
1806                        duplicate = True
1807                        break
1808
1809            if not duplicate:
1810                unique_edges.append(edge)
1811                bbox_row = np.array([[min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y]], dtype=float)
1812                if bbox_array.size == 0:
1813                    bbox_array = bbox_row
1814                else:
1815                    bbox_array = np.vstack((bbox_array, bbox_row))
1816
1817        res = unique_edges
1818
1819    return res

Return edges with congruent duplicates handled.

Candidates are filtered by axis-aligned bounding-box overlap before equal_edges.

Arguments:
  • edges (Sequence[LineType]): Segments (point1, point2).
  • keep_one (bool): If True, keep the first copy of each congruent edge. If False, drop every edge that has a congruent duplicate.
Returns:

list[LineType]: Selected edges.

>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> edges = [((0, 0), (40, 0)), ((40, 0), (0, 0)), ((0, 40), (40, 40))]

def polygon_verts_and_bbox( poly: Union[simetri.shapes.shape.Shape, Sequence[Sequence[float]]]) -> tuple[Sequence[Sequence[float]], float, float, float, float]: 
1822def polygon_verts_and_bbox(
1823    poly: PolygonLike,
1824) -> tuple[Sequence[PointType], float, float, float, float]:
1825    """Return comparison vertices and an axis-aligned bounding box.
1826
1827    For a ``Group``, shared edges are removed and the largest closed
1828    outline is used. If no closed outline is found, ``all_vertices`` is
1829    used instead.
1830
1831    Args:
1832        poly (PolygonLike): A ``Shape``, a ``Group``, or vertex sequence.
1833
1834    Returns:
1835        tuple: ``(vertices, min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y)``.
1836
1837    Examples:
1838        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1839        >>> verts, min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y = sg.polygon_verts_and_bbox(
1840        ... [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
1841        ... )
1842        >>> verts
1843        [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
1844        >>> (min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y)
1845        (0, 0, 40, 40)
1846"""
1847    from ...group.batch import Group
1848    from ...shapes.shape import Shape
1849
1850    if isinstance(poly, Group):
1851        sw = poly.b_box.southwest
1852        ne = poly.b_box.northeast
1853        min_x, min_y = sw[0], sw[1]
1854        max_x, max_y = ne[0], ne[1]
1855        boundary_edges = remove_duplicate_edges(poly.all_edges, keep_one=False)
1856        merged = Group([Shape(edge) for edge in boundary_edges]).merge_shapes()
1857        verts = []
1858        largest_area = -1
1859        for shape in merged:
1860            if (
1861                isinstance(shape, Shape)
1862                and shape.closed
1863                and shape.area > largest_area
1864            ):
1865                largest_area = shape.area
1866                verts = list(shape.vertices)
1867        if not verts:
1868            verts = poly.all_vertices
1869    elif isinstance(poly, Shape):
1870        verts = list(poly.vertices)
1871        sw = poly.b_box.southwest
1872        ne = poly.b_box.northeast
1873        min_x, min_y = sw[0], sw[1]
1874        max_x, max_y = ne[0], ne[1]
1875    else:
1876        verts = list(poly)
1877        xs = [p[0] for p in verts]
1878        ys = [p[1] for p in verts]
1879        min_x, min_y = min(xs), min(ys)
1880        max_x, max_y = max(xs), max(ys)
1881
1882    return verts, min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y

Return comparison vertices and an axis-aligned bounding box.

For a Group, shared edges are removed and the largest closed outline is used. If no closed outline is found, all_vertices is used instead.

Arguments:
  • poly (PolygonLike): A Shape, a Group, or vertex sequence.
Returns:

tuple: (vertices, min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y).

Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> verts, min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y = sg.polygon_verts_and_bbox(
... [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
... )
>>> verts
[(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
>>> (min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y)
(0, 0, 40, 40)
def remove_duplicate_polygons( polygons: Sequence[typing.Union[simetri.shapes.shape.Shape, Sequence[Sequence[float]]]], mirror: bool = True, keep_one: bool = True) -> list[typing.Union[simetri.shapes.shape.Shape, Sequence[Sequence[float]]]]: 
1885def remove_duplicate_polygons(
1886    polygons: Sequence[PolygonLike],
1887    mirror: bool = True,
1888    keep_one: bool = True,
1889) -> list[PolygonLike]:
1890    """Return polygons with congruent duplicates removed.
1891
1892    Polygons are grouped by vertex count. Only polygons whose shortest
1893    edge lengths match are compared with :func:`congruent_polygons`.
1894
1895    Args:
1896        polygons (Sequence[PolygonLike]): ``Shape`` objects or vertex
1897            sequences. Groups are not accepted.
1898        mirror (bool): If True, treat reflections as duplicates.
1899        keep_one (bool): If True, keep the first of each congruent class.
1900            If False, drop every polygon that has a congruent partner.
1901
1902    Returns:
1903        list[PolygonLike]: Selected polygon objects from ``polygons``.
1904
1905    Examples:
1906        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1907        >>> square = [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
1908        >>> same = [(40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40), (0, 0)]
1909        >>> tri = [(0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 80)]
1910        >>> sg.remove_duplicate_polygons([square, same, tri])
1911        [[(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], [(0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 80)]]
1912        >>> sg.remove_duplicate_polygons([square, same], keep_one=False)
1913        []
1914"""
1915    abs_tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
1916    entries = []
1917    by_n: dict[int, list[int]] = defaultdict(list)
1918
1919    for i, poly in enumerate(polygons):
1920        verts = polygon_vertices(poly)
1921        turns = rotate_turns_to_min_edge(polygon_turns(verts))
1922        start_len = turns[0] if turns else 0.0
1923        entries.append(
1924            {
1925                "poly": poly,
1926                "turns": turns,
1927                "start_len": start_len,
1928            }
1929        )
1930        by_n[len(verts)].append(i)
1931
1932    def _same_start_len(i: int, j: int) -> bool:
1933        return isclose(
1934            entries[i]["start_len"],
1935            entries[j]["start_len"],
1936            rel_tol=0.0,
1937            abs_tol=abs_tol,
1938        )
1939
1940    def _are_congruent(i: int, j: int) -> bool:
1941        if not _same_start_len(i, j):
1942            return False
1943        return congruent_polygons(
1944            entries[i]["poly"],
1945            entries[j]["poly"],
1946            mirror=mirror,
1947        )
1948
1949    n = len(polygons)
1950    if n == 0:
1951        return []
1952
1953    if keep_one:
1954        keep = [True] * n
1955        for indices in by_n.values():
1956            kept_in_group: list[int] = []
1957            for i in indices:
1958                if any(_are_congruent(i, j) for j in kept_in_group):
1959                    keep[i] = False
1960                else:
1961                    kept_in_group.append(i)
1962        res = [polygons[i] for i in range(n) if keep[i]]
1963    else:
1964        has_duplicate = [False] * n
1965        for indices in by_n.values():
1966            for a, i in enumerate(indices):
1967                for j in indices[a + 1 :]:
1968                    if _are_congruent(i, j):
1969                        has_duplicate[i] = True
1970                        has_duplicate[j] = True
1971        res = [polygons[i] for i in range(n) if not has_duplicate[i]]
1972
1973    return res

Return polygons with congruent duplicates removed.

Polygons are grouped by vertex count. Only polygons whose shortest edge lengths match are compared with congruent_polygons().

Arguments:
  • polygons (Sequence[PolygonLike]): Shape objects or vertex sequences. Groups are not accepted.
  • mirror (bool): If True, treat reflections as duplicates.
  • keep_one (bool): If True, keep the first of each congruent class. If False, drop every polygon that has a congruent partner.
Returns:

list[PolygonLike]: Selected polygon objects from polygons.

Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> square = [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
>>> same = [(40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40), (0, 0)]
>>> tri = [(0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 80)]
>>> sg.remove_duplicate_polygons([square, same, tri])
[[(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], [(0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 80)]]
>>> sg.remove_duplicate_polygons([square, same], keep_one=False)
[]
def symmetric_difference( shapes: simetri.group.batch.Group, length_bound: int = 10) -> tuple[Sequence[simetri.shapes.shape.Shape], simetri.shapes.shape.Shape]: 
1976def symmetric_difference(
1977    shapes: Group, length_bound: int = 10
1978) -> tuple[Sequence[Shape], Shape]:
1979    """Return the filled faces of the symmetric difference of overlapping shapes.
1980
1981    This calls :func:`get_partitions` and :func:`set_fills`.
1982
1983    Args:
1984        shapes (Group): Overlapping polygon shapes.
1985        length_bound (int): Maximum cycle length for face enumeration.
1986            Defaults to 10.
1987
1988    Returns:
1989        tuple[Sequence[Shape], Shape]: Filled partitions and their union
1990        outline.
1991
1992    Examples:
1993        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1994        >>> square = sg.Shape([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
1995        >>> group = sg.Group([square])
1996        >>> square.closed
1997        True
1998"""
1999    partitions, d_edge_part, union = get_partitions(shapes, length_bound)
2000    set_fills(partitions, d_edge_part)
2001    print(
2002        f"* Largest partition that can be computed with length_bound = {length_bound}."
2003    )

def in_polygon( point: Sequence[float], polygon_vertices: Sequence[Sequence[float]], exclude_border: bool = False) -> bool: 
2007def in_polygon(
2008    point: PointType,
2009    polygon_vertices: Sequence[PointType],
2010    exclude_border: bool = False,
2011) -> bool:
2012    """Return whether a point lies inside a polygon.
2013
2014    Uses the winding number. A point on an edge is inside unless
2015    ``exclude_border`` is True.
2016
2017    Args:
2018        point (PointType): Point ``(x, y)`` to test.
2019        polygon_vertices (Sequence[PointType]): Ordered polygon vertices.
2020        exclude_border (bool): If True, points on an edge return False.
2021            Defaults to False.
2022
2023    Returns:
2024        bool: True if inside, else False.
2025
2026    Examples:
2027        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2028        >>> square = [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
2029        >>> sg.in_polygon((0.5, 0.5), square)
2030        True
2031        >>> sg.in_polygon((0.5, 0), square)
2032        True
2033        >>> sg.in_polygon((0.5, 0), square, exclude_border=True)
2034        False
2035        >>> sg.in_polygon((80, 80), square)
2036        False
2037"""
2038    _, y = point[:2]
2039    n_winding = 0  # Initialize the winding number
2040
2041    n = len(polygon_vertices)
2042    for i_ in range(n):
2043        p1 = polygon_vertices[i_]
2044        p2 = polygon_vertices[(i_ + 1) % n]  # Connect last vertex to first
2045        _, y1 = p1
2046        _, y2 = p2
2047        if point_on_line_segment(point, [p1, p2]):
2048            return not exclude_border
2049        if y1 <= y:  # Start y <= P.y
2050            if y2 > y and left3(p1, p2, point):  # An upward crossing
2051                n_winding += 1  # P left of edge
2052        elif y2 <= y and not left3(p1, p2, point):  # A downward crossing
2053            n_winding -= 1  # P right of edge
2054
2055    return n_winding != 0

Return whether a point lies inside a polygon.

Uses the winding number. A point on an edge is inside unless exclude_border is True.

  • polygon_vertices (Sequence[PointType]): Ordered polygon vertices.
  • exclude_border (bool): If True, points on an edge return False. Defaults to False.
Returns:

bool: True if inside, else False.

Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> square = [(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)]
>>> sg.in_polygon((0.5, 0.5), square)

>>> sg.in_polygon((0.5, 0), square)
True
>>> sg.in_polygon((0.5, 0), square, exclude_border=True)
False
>>> sg.in_polygon((80, 80), square)
False

def double_offset_polylines( lines: Sequence[Sequence[float]], offset: float = 1, rel_tol: float | None = None, abs_tol: float | None = None) -> Sequence[Sequence[Sequence[float]]]: 
2082def double_offset_polylines(
2083    lines: Sequence[PointType],
2084    offset: float = 1,
2085    rel_tol: float | None = None,
2086    abs_tol: float | None = None,
2087) -> Sequence[Sequence[PointType]]:
2088    """Return both offset polylines of an open chain of points.
2089
2090    Args:
2091        lines (Sequence[PointType]): Polyline vertices.
2092        offset (float): Offset distance. Defaults to 1.
2093        rel_tol (float | None): Relative stitch tolerance. Defaults to
2094            ``runtime_defaults["rel_tol"]``.
2095        abs_tol (float | None): Absolute stitch tolerance. Defaults to
2096            ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
2097
2098    Returns:
2099        list: ``[positive_offset, negative_offset]``.
2100
2101    Examples:
2102        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2103        >>> sg.double_offset_polylines([(0, 0), (80, 0), (80, 80)], 1)
2104        [[[0.0, 1.0], (79.0, 1.0), [79.0, 80.0]], [[0.0, -1.0], (81.0, -1.0), [81.0, 80.0]]]
2105"""
2106    rel_tol, abs_tol = get_defaults(["rel_tol", "abs_tol"], [rel_tol, abs_tol])
2107    lines1 = []
2108    lines2 = []
2109    for i, point in enumerate(lines[:-1]):
2110        line = [point, lines[i + 1]]
2111        line1, line2 = double_offset_lines(line, offset)
2112        lines1.append(line1)
2113        lines2.append(line2)
2114    lines1 = stitch(lines1, closed=False)
2115    lines2 = stitch(lines2, closed=False)
2116    return [lines1, lines2]

Return both offset polylines of an open chain of points.

Arguments:

def polygon_cg(points: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> Sequence[float] | None: 
2119def polygon_cg(points: Sequence[PointType]) -> PointType | None:
2120    """Return the area center of a polygon.
2121
2122    This is the center of gravity of the filled polygon, not the average
2123    of the vertices. A zero-area ring returns ``None``.
2124
2125    Args:
2126        points (Sequence[PointType]): Vertices in walk order.
2127
2128    Returns:
2129        PointType | None: Area center, or ``None`` if the area is zero.
2130
2131    Examples:
2132        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2133        >>> sg.polygon_cg([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)])
2134        [20.0, 20.0]
2135        >>> sg.polygon_cg([(0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 80)])
2136        [26.666666666666668, 26.666666666666668]
2137        >>> sg.polygon_cg([(0, 0), (40, 0), (80, 0)]) is None
2138        True
2139"""
2140    cx = cy = 0
2141    n_points = len(points)
2142    for i in range(n_points):
2143        x = points[i][0]
2144        y = points[i][1]
2145        xnext = points[(i + 1) % n_points][0]
2146        ynext = points[(i + 1) % n_points][1]
2147
2148        temp = x * ynext - xnext * y
2149        cx += (x + xnext) * temp
2150        cy += (y + ynext) * temp
2151    area_ = polygon_area(points)
2152    denom = area_ * 6
2153    if denom:
2154        res = [cx / denom, cy / denom]
2155    else:
2156        res = None
2157    return res

def offset_polygon( polygon: Sequence[Sequence[float]], offset: float = -1, abs_tol: float | None = None) -> Sequence[Sequence[float]]: 
2160def offset_polygon(
2161    polygon: Sequence[PointType],
2162    offset: float = -1,
2163    abs_tol: float | None = None,
2164) -> Sequence[PointType]:
2165    """Return a closed polygon offset from ``polygon``.
2166
2167    Positive ``offset`` expands outward; negative deflates. The default
2168    ``-1`` therefore shrinks the ring by 1.
2169
2170    Args:
2171        polygon (Sequence[PointType]): Polygon vertices.
2172        offset (float): Offset distance. Defaults to -1.
2173        abs_tol (float | None): Distance used to decide whether the ring
2174            is already closed. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
2175
2176    Returns:
2177        Sequence[PointType]: Closed offset ring.
2178
2179    Examples:
2180        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2181        >>> sg.offset_polygon([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], 0.5)
2182        [(-0.5, -0.5), (40.5, -0.5), (40.5, 40.5), (-0.5, 40.5), (-0.5, -0.5)]
2183"""
2184    if abs_tol is None:
2185        abs_tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
2186    polygon = list(polygon[:])
2187    abs_tol2 = abs_tol * abs_tol
2188    if not right_handed(polygon):
2189        polygon.reverse()
2190    if not close_points_square(polygon[0], polygon[-1], dist2=abs_tol2):
2191        polygon.append(polygon[0])
2192    poly = []
2193    for i, point in enumerate(polygon[:-1]):
2194        line = [point, polygon[i + 1]]
2195        offset_edge = offset_line(line, -offset)
2196        poly.append(offset_edge)
2197
2198    poly = stitch(poly, closed=True)
2199    return poly

def double_offset_polygons( polygon: Sequence[Sequence[float]], offset: float = 1, abs_tol: float | None = None, **kwargs: Any) -> Sequence[Sequence[Sequence[float]]]: 
2202def double_offset_polygons(
2203    polygon: Sequence[PointType],
2204    offset: float = 1,
2205    abs_tol: float | None = None,
2206    **kwargs: Any,
2207) -> Sequence[Sequence[PointType]]:
2208    """Return both offset polygons of a vertex ring.
2209
2210    Args:
2211        polygon (Sequence[PointType]): Polygon vertices. An unclosed ring
2212            is treated as closed, and a clockwise ring is reversed for
2213            the offset calculation.
2214        offset (float): Offset distance. Defaults to 1.
2215        abs_tol (float | None): Distance used to decide whether the ring
2216            is already closed. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
2217        **kwargs (Any): If ``canvas`` is a canvas, both offsets are drawn.
2218
2219    Returns:
2220        list: ``[positive_offset, negative_offset]``.
2221
2222    Examples:
2223        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2224        >>> raw = [(0, 0), (80, 0), (80, 40)]
2225        >>> offsets = sg.double_offset_polygons(raw, 0.5)
2226        >>> raw
2227        [(0, 0), (80, 0), (80, 40)]
2228        >>> offsets[0]
2229        [(2.1180339887498945, 0.5), (79.5, 0.5), (79.5, 39.19098300562505), (2.1180339887498945, 0.5)]
2230        >>> offsets[1]
2231        [(-2.118033988749895, -0.5), (80.5, -0.5), (80.5, 40.80901699437495), (-2.118033988749895, -0.5)]
2232"""
2233    if abs_tol is None:
2234        abs_tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
2235    abs_tol2 = abs_tol * abs_tol
2236
2237    ring = list(polygon)
2238    if not close_points_square(ring[0], ring[-1], dist2=abs_tol2):
2239        ring.append(ring[0])
2240
2241    if not right_handed(ring):
2242        ring.reverse()
2243    poly1 = []
2244    poly2 = []
2245    for i, point in enumerate(ring[:-1]):
2246        line = [point, ring[i + 1]]
2247        line1, line2 = double_offset_lines(line, offset)
2248        poly1.append(line1)
2249        poly2.append(line2)
2250    poly1 = stitch(poly1)
2251    poly2 = stitch(poly2)
2252    if "canvas" in kwargs:
2253        canvas = kwargs["canvas"]
2254        if canvas:
2255            canvas.new_page()
2256            closed = close_points_square(poly1[0], poly1[-1])
2257            canvas.draw(_shape(poly1, closed=closed), fill=False)
2258            closed = close_points_square(poly2[0], poly2[-1])
2259            canvas.draw(_shape(poly2, closed=closed), fill=False)
2260    return [poly1, poly2]

2290def polyline_length(
2291    polygon: Sequence[PointType],
2292    closed: bool = False,
2293    abs_tol: float | None = None,
2294) -> float:
2295    """Return the length of a polyline, or the perimeter if it is closed.
2296
2297    Args:
2298        polygon (Sequence[PointType]): Vertices in order.
2299        closed (bool): If True, include the closing edge when it is missing.
2300            Defaults to False.
2301        abs_tol (float | None): Distance used to decide whether the ring
2302            is already closed. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
2303
2304    Returns:
2305        float: Path length.
2306
2307    Examples:
2308        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2309        >>> sg.polyline_length([(0, 0), (60, 0), (60, 80)])
2310        140.0
2311        >>> sg.polyline_length([(0, 0), (40, 0), (40, 40), (0, 40)], closed=True)
2312        160.0
2313"""
2314    if abs_tol is None:
2315        abs_tol = runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]
2316    abs_tol2 = abs_tol * abs_tol
2317    polygon = list(polygon)
2318    if closed and not close_points_square(
2319        polygon[0], polygon[-1], dist2=abs_tol2
2320    ):
2321        polygon.append(polygon[0])
2322    perimeter = 0
2323    for i, point in enumerate(polygon[:-1]):
2324        perimeter += distance(point, polygon[i + 1])
2325    return perimeter
